mainEntity.name: Do iPhone/iPad and Mac need to be on the same Wi-Fi network?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. NinoPad communicates directly over your high-speed local network (Wi-Fi), requiring no internet or cloud relay for minimal latency and maximum privacy.

mainEntity.name: Why is Mac not responding to key presses or screen stream?

acceptedAnswer.text: Basic hotkeys and cursor control require Accessibility permission in macOS 'System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility'. Screen mirroring requires 'Screen Recording' permission.

mainEntity.name: Are core features free? How do I purchase or restore Pro?

acceptedAnswer.text: All core keypads, trackpad, and system controls are 100% free. Pro membership can be subscribed to or purchased as a lifetime unlock inside the iOS app via Apple StoreKit, with full support for restoring purchases across devices.

mainEntity.name: Is my data or screen content uploaded to the cloud?

acceptedAnswer.text: Never. All control commands, text, and screen streams are transmitted strictly peer-to-peer within your local area network without passing through any external servers.

mainEntity.name: Which Mac devices and operating systems are supported?

acceptedAnswer.text: Supports macOS 13 (Ventura) and later. The Universal binary natively supports both Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4 chips) and Intel-based Macs.

privacy.attr_000: NinoPad Privacy Policy and Data Security Instructions
privacy.text_008: NinoPad uses a pure local area network communication architecture to connect iPhone/iPad and Mac. There is no need to register an account, no need to log in, and no cloud server is used to transfer your control commands or screen images.
privacy.text_010: Your custom keypad layout, pairing credentials, connected device aliases, and app preferences are all securely saved in the device's local sandbox. The main app shares connection state with the iOS desktop widget through a protected App Group.
privacy.text_012: Pro membership purchases, renewals, automatic deductions, cancellations, and refunds are all handled by Apple’s official StoreKit channel. NinoPad only reads verified valid membership rights and will never contact or store any of your bank card information, billing address or Apple account credentials.
privacy.text_014: After you actively turn it on, the personalized keypad layout and settings will be synchronized across devices strictly through your personal Apple iCloud container; NinoPad will never use such data for any analysis or advertising purposes.
privacy.text_015: 5. Local network communication and screen recording
privacy.text_016: The app discovers Mac devices on the same Wi-Fi LAN via Apple's native Bonjour protocol. Control commands are transmitted directly point-to-point; low-latency screen streaming only takes effect after obtaining macOS "Screen Recording" authorization and is only transmitted locally.
privacy.text_018: The Mac side requires the "Accessibility" permission to execute cross-application shortcut keys and mouse commands; the "Screen Recording" and "Microphone" permissions are only requested on demand when screen streaming or wireless microphones are enabled, and you can revoke them at any time in the system settings.
privacy.text_020: The official website provides HTTPS secure static hosting and distribution of the entire site, and the installation package is securely distributed through GitHub Releases. There will never be any third-party advertising SDK or cross-application tracking code embedded in the NinoPad app.

updates.text_032: Continuously polishing every interaction and performance detail to make the handheld secondary controller smoother and more stable
updates.text_036: New official website and game hall are online, Pro supports redemption of discount codes
updates.text_038: Ninopad.com is enabled on the official website, arcade.ninopad.com is enabled in the game lobby, and all entrances automatically use HTTPS; the old official website link will jump to the new URL.
updates.text_039: The Universal installation package for Mac 1.3.6 has been signed and notarized, and supports Apple chips and Intel devices; automatic in-app updates have also been switched to the new GitHub repository.
updates.text_040: iOS 1.3.6 has been submitted to the App Store for review and will be automatically released after passing the review.
updates.text_041: The Pro page adds Apple’s official discount code redemption portal. New users of annual subscriptions can enjoy the first month free with a qualified redemption code; the specific price and renewal terms are subject to Apple’s redemption page.
updates.text_043: The game lobby adds installation and connection tutorials for the Magic Controller, and provides access to the official website and support pages.
updates.text_044: The Mac Game Hall adds a complete game list and improves controller recognition after reconnection.
updates.text_050: Officially launched on the App Store, connecting mobile phones and Mac in one step
updates.text_052: NinoPad is already on the App Store, and the official version can be downloaded directly for iPhone and iPad without the need to install it through TestFlight.
updates.text_053: The current official version of the App Store is 1.3.2, and the Mac version is 1.3.4; each version is updated as an independent version.
updates.text_055: The mobile download portal in the menu bar, pairing interface, and settings has been enabled. You can directly open the App Store, scan the QR code to download, or copy the link.
updates.text_056: Download the QR code to install the mobile app; after installation, scan the Mac’s pairing QR code in the mobile app to complete the connection.
updates.text_058: The official website homepage, download area, support guide and footer supplement the App Store official download entrance, retaining the existing design and tutorial structure.
updates.text_059: Mac can check for updates through the app or download a signed, notarized Universal installation package; supports Apple chips and Intel devices running macOS 13 and above.
updates.text_060: The official version of iPhone/iPad requires iOS/iPadOS 17 and above. When connecting to your Mac, make sure both ends are on the same LAN.
updates.text_065: Put your programming assistant at your fingertips: a new atmospheric programming workbench
updates.text_067: The new "Ambient Programming" workbench: extends the Mac programming assistant to the desktop. It supports quick switching between project files and multiple sessions, task queuing and editing, on-demand reading of long replies and preview of deliverables. You can follow usage and confirm operation permissions in real time at your fingertips (actual test adapts to Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity).
updates.text_068: The original layout was renamed "Codex": focusing on reading back the status of the 6 task slots of the Codex, native quota and inference adjustment, the positioning is clearer.
updates.text_069: Small screen display optimization: Fixed the black background overflow in the four corners of the small screen preview in the layout, and the picture and the rounded border fit correctly.
updates.text_070: Upgraded pocket sampling and instrument experience: Optimize the response of 16 drum pad slices and the interactive feel of the sequencer, improving the stability and sound performance of the offline audio engine.
updates.text_075: Synthesizers, guitars and dynamic wallpapers give your phone more ways to play
updates.text_076: Synthesizer: from a chord to an arrangement
updates.text_077: Four new desktops have been added: Chord, Tone, Arrangement, and Loop. Play with the seventh-level chord keys and joystick, adjust the tone, and edit drum beats, chords, bass, and melodies.
updates.text_078: The six-track loop supports recording, overdubbing, undoing, and mixing; projects can be saved, restored, and exported to WAV or MIDI.
updates.text_079: Sound material can be exchanged with sample layouts; MIDI output is optional when connected to a Mac. The sound can be played on the mobile phone, and there is no need to pair the computer first for basic performance.
updates.text_080: Improved audio peak protection, long project saving and recording ending, reducing unnecessary refreshes when switching interfaces.
updates.text_081: Guitar: strum, change chords, and learn step by step
updates.text_082: Two new desktops, Guitar and Learning, have been added. Six sensor strings, eight-way chord rocker, mute keys and bend strip can be combined and played.
updates.text_083: The console supports editing chords, tunings, capos, voices and left- and right-handed orientations, saving your own solutions and listening to them before switching.
updates.text_084: The learning desktop provides 100 harmony exercises, selected according to style and difficulty; listen to the demonstration first, and then practice step by step following the string positions and chord tips. The content is an independently arranged short exercise, not an original recording or complete score.
updates.text_085: Improved anti-accidental touch, playback stop and background recovery during strumming, retaining clear operation feedback.
updates.text_087: There are eight built-in animal dynamic wallpapers, which can be searched by name and can also be set individually for different layouts.
updates.text_088: Custom wallpapers support importing images, videos and animations from photos or file multiple selections; Live Photo can read dynamic parts from the photo library.
updates.text_089: The wallpaper list supports reuse, renaming and removal, and provides three levels of import quality: energy-saving, balanced, and clear, and the option to only display the cover.
updates.text_090: Live wallpapers play silently and retain static covers in the background, low battery, or weakened dynamic effects. Videos of layouts used alone can be exported with the workbench.
updates.text_091: The operating experience works with Mac
updates.text_092: Improved presentation pointer position updating and drawing, optimized trackpad, continuous controls, and feedback on touch release.
updates.text_093: Improved Mac MIDI message handling and muting behavior for synthesizers and guitars.
updates.text_094: The official website page is organized into 17 sets of layouts according to purpose, supplemented with actual app screenshots and introductory tutorials of new functions.
updates.text_096: iPhone/iPad updates via TestFlight; on Mac, check for updates in-app or download a new version of DMG.
updates.text_097: It is recommended that mobile phones and Macs be updated to 1.3.0 together. The minimum system requirements are still iOS/iPadOS 17, macOS 13.
updates.text_098: This Mac installation package follows the configuration of the previous version and does not include the system virtual controller that requires additional authorization; the in-app game lobby and MIDI can still be used.
updates.text_103: 15 preset layouts covering work, creation and daily life
updates.text_105: Work, Launcher, Browser, Media, Presentation, Ambient Programming, Terminal, Writing, Research, Reading, Finance, Application Creation Bench, Sampling, Gaming and Smart Home. Some layouts contain multiple desktops with the ability to edit position, size, color, and motion.
updates.text_107: Terminal: Create a standalone shell on a paired Mac with session tabs, full screen, font size, and Chinese input, retaining up to 8 sessions per device.
updates.text_108: Writing: Dual desktops for text and format, move and select by word, word, sentence, and paragraph; new title slider, Markdown format, search, and word count. Precision editing with Obsidian requires the installation of the included plug-in.
updates.text_109: Scientific research and reading: classified collection of selected articles, notes and actual sources; PDF, EPUB and web page turning, scroll wheel, table of contents and chapter jump. See the official website guide for the capabilities and verification scope of different readers.
updates.text_110: Finance: Numeric keypad, local calculator, 28 table shortcuts and four pages of 64 formulas. Click to enter the formula, long press to fill in the parameters; send text to the current application on Mac without reading the workbook or automatically submitting.
updates.text_111: Smart home: The mobile phone is directly connected to the existing Home Assistant or Apple home, and the device capabilities are added to the editable layout; a Mac is not required, and the Matter device needs to be connected to the corresponding home platform first.
updates.text_112: Launcher: Read Mac application icons and Dock order, support editing of multiple desktops and application buttons.
updates.text_113: Unified clipboard: collection and input history, text/website/picture/file filtering, album multi-selection, batch export and keyboard draft recovery.
updates.text_114: Presentation: The phone screen and camera can be transferred to the Mac presentation window to supplement the speech aid, page turning and timing desktop.
updates.text_115: Sampling: local sound library, slicing and 16-frame performance combination, adding mobile phone and Mac sound collection entrance, improving recording, saving and exporting.
updates.text_117: The media layout unifies the information screen and click wheel navigation, and adds playback queue, progress positioning, sound output and timed pause; the menu is displayed according to the actual capabilities of the player.
updates.text_118: The application creation platform expands software adaptation, organizes the core operations of clipping/CapCut, and improves numerical focus switching and continuous knob gesture recovery.
updates.text_119: Preset text, desktop automation, action recording and hotkey triggering can be configured to layout keys.
updates.text_120: Added wallpaper selection and layout appearance settings, improved layout browsing, native paging and button editing.
updates.text_121: Fixed issues in browser input and URL copying, clip filtering, formula parameter group deletion, and recording and streaming status management.
updates.text_123: This Mac installation package does not include the virtual HID controller yet: Apple still needs to grant the corresponding Developer ID permission. Keyboard and mouse control and other functions are not subject to this restriction.
updates.text_124: It is recommended that iOS and Mac be updated at the same time. iOS/iPadOS 17+, macOS 13+; Mac installation package includes Apple Silicon and Intel architecture.
updates.text_125: The new clipboard uses a separate local database and does not automatically import old keyboard history or old excerpts. Please copy or export the old content that needs to be retained before upgrading.
updates.text_126: Sampling local performances, calculators and home controls each have independent usage conditions; software adaptation, lyrics, document directories and device controls are subject to actual capabilities.
updates.text_127: The Pro functions and prices within the app are subject to those shown on the purchase page. The demo data in the official website guide is only used to display the interface.
updates.text_132: The small keyboard automatically switches to the editing workbench with the software
updates.text_134: For DaVinci Resolve, Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro and Cut Pro, the same set of physical knobs and buttons automatically switches with the current front-end software.
updates.text_136: Added real-time keys, commonly used shortcut commands and direction key controls.
updates.text_138: Added live sound effects such as applause and cheers, and supports custom audio import.
updates.text_140: Focus circle selection supports 4-level radius adjustment, and interactive expressions and barrages support sliding preview.
updates.text_143: The intelligent teleprompter scrolls more smoothly, allowing long sentences and core arguments to stay for a few seconds longer, making the speech more calm.
updates.text_144: The virtual laser pointer has micro-motion filtering and optimization, making slow-speed aiming more stable.
updates.text_145: The clipping knob is protected against accidental touches and automatically pauses smoothly when switching focus.
updates.text_147: Reconstruct the background communication architecture and significantly reduce the macOS system permission application threshold.
updates.text_148: Fixed the issue of slight jitter in the interface when loading some widgets.
updates.text_153: Voice text pre-editing and speech control upgrade
updates.text_155: Presentation tools include a new smart teleprompter, screen drawing board and interactive components.
updates.text_156: The iOS side adopts a new voice transcription architecture, which makes the response faster and more stable.
updates.text_158: The text keyboard supports "dictating, manually modifying, and then continuing dictating", and the modified content will not be overwritten.
updates.text_159: Improve the mobile refresh rate of laser pointers and screen magnifiers on 4K/5K HD external monitors.
updates.text_161: Fixed the issue of cursor jumping when voice input is paused or modified.
updates.text_165: Pro membership and a full set of presentation aids are now available
updates.text_167: Pro membership is officially launched, supporting weekly subscriptions, annual subscriptions and one-time permanent buyouts.
updates.text_168: Added touch and somatosensory dual-mode laser pointers, partial magnifiers and wireless graffiti drawing pads.
updates.text_169: The text keyboard supports searching draft history and air-sending notes to Mac.
updates.text_171: The clear image quality streaming engine is online, making small text on the Mac desktop clearer and sharper.
updates.text_172: Enhanced LAN automatic reconnection stability and media control response speed.
updates.text_176: Mac Preferences and Smart Adaptation Panel
updates.text_178: A new preference panel has been added to the Mac side, which supports auto-starting and checking for updates.
updates.text_179: Supports individually enabling/disabling keypads for different applications and adjusting knob sensitivity.
updates.text_181: Optimize the automatic reconnection mechanism under LAN network fluctuations, making network disconnection and reconnection faster.
updates.text_183: Fixed an issue where window control occasionally became unresponsive in a multi-monitor environment.
updates.text_187: Free keypad canvas and multi-page management are launched
updates.text_189: The "Free Keyboard Editor" is fully launched, supporting grid drag and drop arrangement, key size adjustment and color matching.
updates.text_190: Added new desktop paging management function, supporting left and right swiping to quickly turn pages.
updates.text_191: Added combination of shortcut keys and common script action bindings.
updates.text_193: The underlying network protocol is upgraded to local P2P direct connection, with lower round-trip latency.
updates.text_194: Added official preset templates such as DaVinci Resolve and Final Cut Pro.
updates.text_197: Check out earlier historical releases at GitHub Releases

blog_custom-keypad.text_033: NinoPad allows you to turn your idle iPhone or iPad into a handy Mac exclusive sub-console. Whether you need to quickly send frequently used copywriting, trigger high-frequency shortcut keys with one click, or adapt professional software through the "Application Creation Station", you can freely customize it through the visual desktop editor.
blog_custom-keypad.text_034: This article will take you starting from a basic preset and gradually master the complete process of entering editing mode, adding buttons, configuring width and height, binding specific actions, and adjusting appearance styles.
blog_custom-keypad.text_035: When using it for the first time, it is recommended to start with the built-in "work" or "launcher" and other preset layouts. After getting familiar with the basic interactions, you can add and delete buttons as needed.
blog_custom-keypad.text_037: 1. Start exploring from the preset layout
blog_custom-keypad.text_038: NinoPad has built-in multiple scene presets covering daily office work, browser management, multimedia broadcast control, code development and design creation. In the "Layout" list at the bottom of the app, you can click directly to enter any plan to try.
blog_custom-keypad.text_039: 2. Enter the current desktop editing mode
blog_custom-keypad.text_040: Click at the bottom of the app
blog_custom-keypad.text_041: , enter the desktop editor. Select the component you want to adjust before modifying its position, appearance, or operation.
blog_custom-keypad.text_043: You can long press and drag the button to adjust its position in the grid;
blog_custom-keypad.text_045: , select "Button", and configure the action for the new button.
blog_custom-keypad.text_047: Tap an existing button to open the appearance and property configuration panel.
blog_custom-keypad.text_049: Select a preset from the layout list and enter the editor for the current desktop.
blog_custom-keypad.text_050: 3. Add buttons and set size width and height
blog_custom-keypad.text_051: NinoPad supports freely adjusting the grid size of each component. In the Dimensions area of the appearance settings:
blog_custom-keypad.text_052: It supports 1 to 8 grid widths when held horizontally, and 1 to 4 grid widths when held vertically;
blog_custom-keypad.text_056: Depending on how frequently the keys are pressed, you can set them as small, single-frame icons, or as wide, large keys and multi-line display panels.
blog_custom-keypad.text_058: In the component action configuration panel, you can specify specific execution logic for the button:
blog_custom-keypad.text_059: Enter frequently used replies, customer service copy or frequently used code snippets, and set whether to append a carriage return after input;
blog_custom-keypad.text_064: Single key or combination shortcut keys;
blog_custom-keypad.text_066: Search and bind commonly used software installed on Mac to achieve one-click awakening;
blog_custom-keypad.text_068: Execute text input, delayed waiting and shortcut key combinations in series.
blog_custom-keypad.text_070: 5. Adjust color, shape and icon appearance
blog_custom-keypad.text_071: To make the control panel clear at a glance, you can set rich visual styles for buttons:
blog_custom-keypad.text_072: Choose an easily distinguishable color for your buttons. The launcher's app button can also use a "Follow App" color scheme.
blog_custom-keypad.text_074: Supports various contour switching such as rounded square, circle and rounded diamond;
blog_custom-keypad.text_076: Choose functional symbols from the built-in icon library, or keep the display as text-only.

blog_custom-keypad.text_080: Save configuration. Open the target document or software on your Mac and tap the keys on your phone to test the response.

blog_editing-keypad.text_034: When editing videos, frequently moving back and forth between the keyboard, mouse, and timeline can easily interrupt the creative rhythm. Through NinoPad's "Application Creation Station", you can place your phone next to the keyboard and complete timeline zooming, notch positioning and playback control with one hand.
blog_editing-keypad.text_035: Whether you are using professional DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, Premiere Pro, or daily light editing, NinoPad can provide quick control for front-end software.
blog_editing-keypad.text_036: First use the practice project to familiarize yourself with frame-by-frame browsing and playback, and then try operations that modify clips. The controls available may vary between software and workspaces.
blog_editing-keypad.text_038: 1. First enter the application creation platform and confirm the current editing software.
blog_editing-keypad.text_039: When you open a supported editing software on your Mac and enter the "Application Creation Station", the system will automatically recognize the software environment and display the corresponding operations. Taking video clipping as an example, the commonly supported operations include:
blog_editing-keypad.text_040: Timeline zoom, fit to timeline, previous notch and next notch;
blog_editing-keypad.text_042: Frame-by-frame fine-tuning (previous frame/next frame) and notch positioning;
blog_editing-keypad.text_044: Split segments, delete selections, undo and redo;
blog_editing-keypad.text_046: Play/pause switching and adding key markers.
blog_editing-keypad.text_049: The clipping interface in the application creation platform; when using it, the controls provided in the current workspace shall prevail.
blog_editing-keypad.text_050: Two and three steps of safe practical exercises
blog_editing-keypad.text_051: In order to familiarize yourself with the feel without affecting the ongoing formal project, it is recommended to create a new test project containing a short test fragment and perform the following three-step exercise:
blog_editing-keypad.text_052: Open the test timeline on your Mac and make sure the clipping window has focus.
blog_editing-keypad.text_053: Step 1: Select the test timeline segment
blog_editing-keypad.text_054: Tap the "Previous Frame" or "Next Frame" button on your phone and observe whether the Mac playhead aligns with the screen jump point.
blog_editing-keypad.text_055: Step 2: Small frame-by-frame movement and notch positioning
blog_editing-keypad.text_056: Press the "Play/Pause" preview screen on your phone, tap "Split" to cut the test clip, then press the "Undo" button to restore, and confirm that the shortcut keys respond normally.

blog_guide-automation-steps.text_036: After memorizing a sentence, do you still have to manually press the shortcut key to save it? In fact, just pack multiple actions into the same button. This tutorial will take you to expand a single step into a complete macro of "enter text → pause for 0.5 seconds → automatically press ⌘S". Through mobile phone preview and practical trial operation, you can master the core logic of multi-step automation.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_037: The screenshots show the three steps of real editing in the app and the content preview. The Mac connection status is demo data. The preview does not press ⌘S and does not prove that the file has been saved; the actual saving results need to be checked in your own Mac document.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_040: First read the tutorial on common text buttons and create a "Send Text" button.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_041: Prepare a test document on your Mac that has been saved to disk, and confirm that the software saves it with ⌘S; place the cursor in the editable text.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_042: Connect to the Mac Automation Service; keep "Run Once" for the first exercise to avoid multiple rounds of input that are difficult to judge.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_043: 1. Expand from text buttons to automation
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_044: Open a configured text button in the desktop editing state, and set the input content to "Today's record: confirm the goal first, then add the next step." After input, keep "No additional keys". Close the text editing page, return to the operation configuration panel, and click "Expand to Automation".
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_045: The newly opened "Edit Automation" page will automatically retain the original text steps. Enter "Record and Save" in the "Automation Name" field. This allows you to add subsequent steps from an already defined action without having to retype the entire paragraph.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_047: Complete steps to create commonly used text buttons
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_049: Click "Add step" under "Steps" and select "Wait". The default waiting time for a new step is 0.5 seconds. This example uses this recommended default value directly; if changes are needed, click "Wait 0.5 seconds" to enter the step editing page for fine-tuning.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_050: The list of steps at this time is "Enter text" and "Wait 0.5 seconds". The waiting time is fixed and will not detect whether the target software has been loaded. Appropriate delay waiting can effectively prevent the key conflict caused by the text of the previous step not being fully received by the editor and the shortcut keys of the next step being triggered in advance.
blog_guide-automation-steps.attr_051: After expanding from text actions, add a real "wait 0.5 seconds" step.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_052: After expanding from text actions, add a real "wait 0.5 seconds" step.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_054: Click "Add Step" again, select "Shortcut Key", and then open the newly added shortcut key step. Select "Command" in the key combination area, fill in S in the primary key input box, and complete the input.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_055: Return to the automation editing page and check that the key values displayed in the third step strictly correspond to Command and S. The key combination is sent to the current foreground application of the computer when this step is performed, so the test document needs to be kept in the foreground; the first save as dialog box will change the subsequent process. It is recommended to create and save the test file on Mac first.
blog_guide-automation-steps.attr_056: Select Command in the shortcut key step and fill in the primary key S.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_057: Select Command in the shortcut key step and fill in the primary key S.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_058: 4. Confirm the sequence and set it to "Run Once"
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_059: Go back to the step list and double-check the order of the steps: Step 1 is "Enter text," Step 2 is "Wait 0.5 seconds," and Step 3 is "Command + S." Select "Run once" as the execution mode.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_060: If you add extra steps by mistake, you can use the editor's editing mode to delete or drag and move steps, or you can use the "Undo" button at the bottom to restore recent modifications; if you need to temporarily skip a step, enter the step and turn off "Enable this step".
blog_guide-automation-steps.attr_061: The three steps are sequenced; a run processes the enabled steps in sequence.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_062: The three steps are sequenced; a run processes the enabled steps in sequence.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_063: 5. Preview the content and try it out on Mac
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_064: Click "Preview Content" and check whether the descriptions of the exercise text, wait 0.5 seconds, and save shortcut keys are accurate one by one. Close the preview after confirming that there are no redundant Enter or blank steps.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_065: When connecting to the automation service, you can click "Try Run Once". It saves the configuration and actually executes a round on the Mac's current application. Bring the test document to the foreground before triggering the test run; a record should be inserted and processed by the target software ⌘S. Finally, check the document content and the save status of the software, and if necessary, close and reopen the test file to confirm.
blog_guide-automation-steps.attr_066: The native content preview lists text, wait, and shortcut keys; here it is only previewed and no computer operations are performed.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_067: The native content preview lists text, wait, and shortcut keys; here it is only previewed and no computer operations are performed.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_068: 6. Save button, used in daily documents
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_069: After confirming that the trial run results are as expected, click "Save and Sync" to exit component properties and desktop editing mode. Then just tap the automation button on the mobile phone's sub-controller to complete log appending and instant saving with one click.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_070: For use with other professional software, you can gradually add "switch applications" or more shortcut keys. A trial run is performed for each new step. It is easier to troubleshoot positioning problems than adding a large number of actions at once. First use clear text and shortcut keys to complete a stable small process, and then gradually expand it.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_072: Why does the "Save As" window appear after running it?
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_073: The test file has not completed its first save, or the target software uses ⌘S for other commands. Save the file manually first, confirm the software's shortcut key behavior, then return to the text and try again.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_074: Even after adding wait, why is the word still entered at the wrong position?
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_075: Waiting only pauses for a fixed duration and does not correct focus. Check the Mac foreground application, document body, and pop-up windows; when you need to switch applications, you should explicitly configure the "Switch Application" step.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_076: There is command,s in the preview, why is the file not saved?
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_077: The content preview shows step descriptions and does not execute shortcut keys. It is necessary to test run after connection and confirm the saving result in the target software.
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_078: How do I stop an automation that is running repeatedly?
blog_guide-automation-steps.text_079: The editor provides Stop Automation during runtime; Stop Automation can also be configured as a separate button. The first exercise remains "Run Once" without enabling repeat mode.

mainEntity.name: Why does a 'Save As' dialog appear when executing the macro?

acceptedAnswer.text: The target document has never been saved initially, or the active software maps ⌘S to a different command. Manually save the file once first, verify the app's hotkey behavior, and re-run.

mainEntity.name: Why was text typed into the wrong window even with a delay step?

acceptedAnswer.text: Delays only pause execution for a fixed duration; they do not switch window focus. Ensure your Mac target app and document cursor are focused, or add an explicit 'Switch App' step.

mainEntity.name: Why didn't the document save when preview shows 'command, s'?

acceptedAnswer.text: The on-screen preview describes step definitions without executing actual system shortcuts. Connect to your Mac and test run the button to verify file saving.

mainEntity.name: How do I stop an automation that is running in a loop?

acceptedAnswer.text: The editor provides a 'Stop Automation' button during execution; you can also configure a dedicated emergency stop button. For initial practice, keep the mode set to 'Run Once'.

blog_guide-clipping-export.text_036: As you have accumulated a lot of data, you don’t need to back it up in full every time. Filter by combining search terms with URLs, pictures, and other types, and check target items across conditions to export standardized and organized text and attachments through the system sharing panel, making data review and cross-software organization more refreshing and efficient.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_037: The accompanying picture shows the filtering, selection and system sharing panels of three local practice collections in the App. Which directory to save to finally needs to be selected on your own device.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_040: Open Clips from the Study Layout; the bulk Select entry is in the Clips list.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_041: First create three practice collections: meeting list, source link check, and screenshot arrangement for next week. They are all tutorial material only.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_042: This article demonstrates pure text export; items with existing attachments will bring out the original attachments at the same time, and you can preview the file before exporting.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_044: Click "New Collection" one by one according to the following content and save it. In the second article, add the source title "NinoPad Study Tutorial" and the link https://ninopad.com/blog/layout-research in the "Source".
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_045: After saving, there should be three items in the list. The common keyword of the first two is "Friday review", and the third is only used to confirm that the screening has indeed excluded irrelevant content.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_046: Meeting list: Text "Friday review: Organize meeting issues into a list."; Notes "Project Alpha, confirm the person in charge for the next meeting.".
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_047: Source check: Text "Friday Review: Update clipped source link."; fill in the above source title and link.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_048: Next week's schedule: Text "Next week's schedule: Arrange screenshots on Tuesday."; note "Project Beta".
blog_guide-clipping-export.attr_049: The three exercises are created and saved in the app by scripts.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_050: The three exercises are created and saved in the app by scripts.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_051: 2. Combine search and content type, look for linked material first
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_052: Enter "Friday review" in the search box and confirm that only the first two are left. Click "Website" in the content type again, and you should only see the "Update Clip Source Link" item.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_053: There are two levels of filtering here: "All/Collection/History" at the top determines the content range, and the content type determines the URL, image, file or text to be viewed; the search terms will continue to narrow the scope. This example entry with a source URL can be filtered by "Website".
blog_guide-clipping-export.attr_054: The "Friday Review" and "Website" conditions are effective together, and only the practice material with the source link is displayed.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_055: The "Friday Review" and "Website" conditions are effective together, and only the practice material with the source link is displayed.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_056: 3. Select the first item, then switch the filter to add the second item
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_057: Click "Select" in the upper right corner and check the source check item. Then switch the content type back to "All Types", keep the search terms, and check the meeting list. The bottom should say "Export(2)".
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_058: Switching filters will not clear selected items. This behavior is suitable for finding images first, then text, and exporting them together, but it also means that the number of entries seen on the current screen may be less than the actual number selected. Before clicking export, check it based on the bottom quantity.
blog_guide-clipping-export.attr_059: After selecting across content types, "Export (2)" at the bottom confirms that two items have been selected this time.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_060: After selecting across content types, "Export (2)" at the bottom confirms that two items have been selected this time.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_061: 4. Open the export and select the storage location in the system sharing panel.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_062: Click "Export (2)" and wait for the system sharing panel to appear. To leave a file that can be inspected, select "Save to 'File'" or the synonymous option currently displayed by the system, then select a directory and complete the save.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_063: The apps, languages, and system versions installed on different devices will affect the sharing panel options. When selecting a receiving app, the file receiving method it actually supports shall prevail; the screenshots in this article show the prepared export content and system panel.
blog_guide-clipping-export.attr_064: The app is ready to export files and open the native iOS sharing panel; the final directory needs to be selected by yourself.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_065: The app is ready to export files and open the native iOS sharing panel; the final directory needs to be selected by yourself.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_066: 5. Check the exported text, notes and sources
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_067: Go to the directory you just selected and open the exported .txt file. In this example, there should be two entries: one containing the meeting text and "Notes", and the other containing the source check text and the title and URL in "Source". File numbers are generated in the order of entries when exported, and do not have to be consistent with the order listed in this article.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_068: If the entry also has attachments, the original attachments will be exported together as independent files; when the same underlying attachment is used by multiple entries, duplication will be removed, and suffixes will be added to distinguish files with the same name but different files. Therefore, "selecting two files" does not necessarily mean "exporting only two files".
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_069: 6. Understand the scope of “select all” and avoid bringing out unnecessary content
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_070: In selection mode, "Select All" will select all items in the current filter results, including items that require scrolling to see. "Unselect all" will only cancel this batch of results, and the checked content under other filtering conditions will still be retained.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_071: When the number of selections is not as expected, click "Cancel" in the upper left corner to exit the selection mode, clear the check box, and then select again. Exporting only generates a copy of the file and does not delete the original collection; after saving, open the file first and confirm that the required text, notes, sources, and attachments are all there.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_073: Complete notes and references for clipping
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_075: Why does the export quantity not return to zero after changing the filter conditions?
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_076: This is the behavior of cross-filter selections. Selected items will remain; check with the bottom number, or exit selection mode and select again.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_077: Is the export a fully recoverable database backup?
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_078: What is exported is an easy-to-read .txt text file and the original attachment, suitable for archiving or sending to other software. It is not a full database backup that can be restored with one click.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_080: Start by going to the "Clips" folder from the study layout and making sure there are entries. The history records in the keyboard are mainly used for backfill input, not the batch sorting entry demonstrated in this article.
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_081: Why are the number of exported files and the number of selections different?
blog_guide-clipping-export.text_082: Each piece of content may generate a text file with multiple attachments; duplicate attachments will be deduplicated. Check the entry text and attachment name first, don't just compare the quantity.

blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_040: Open the study layout and click "Clip" to enter the list; you can also refer to the study layout tutorial to find the entry.
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_041: Prepare a text that is allowed to be saved, as well as its actual corresponding source title and link.
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_042: The source link of the exercises in this article points to the NinoPad Magic Control Study Tutorial; the exercise sentences themselves are not quotes from the original text of the page.
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_043: 1. Create a new collection and fill in the excerpt
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_044: Click "New Collection" in the upper right corner of the Clips main interface. In the text area, enter "Tutorial exercise: first check the original text, and then write your own summary."
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_045: The main text is suitable for excerpts, and your own understanding and to-do items are left in the notes area, making it easier to distinguish when looking back. The top of the page also provides entrances for photo albums, files, and pasting; this time, save the plain text first, and then add attachments according to the data type after you are familiar with it.
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_047: Study the clipping entry in the layout
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_048: 2. Open your notes and write down your thoughts
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_049: Click "Notes" to expand the input area and write an action memo for the material, such as "Friday review: Check whether the source link is complete."
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_050: Notes do not need to mechanically repeat the main text. You can write specific next steps such as "check the page number before quoting" and "compare with the previous version of the plan." Each note has a length limit. If the page prompts that the length exceeds the limit, please refine and streamline it before saving. Take another look before saving: keep excerpts of the text and your own thoughts on the notes, which will be easier to distinguish when exporting later.
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_051: 3. Fill in the source and save the information
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_052: Scroll down and expand the "Sources" section. Fill in the source title as "NinoPad Magic Control Study Tutorial" and fill in the source link as https://ninopad.com/blog/layout-research.
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_053: Real material should be replaced with the actual page address, and you cannot just write the search engine homepage or complete the title based on impressions. Click "Save" in the upper right corner, and a "Tutorial Exercise" entry containing a summary of the notes should appear after returning to the list.

blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_055: The actual saved clip list, practice text and note summary are all visible.

blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_057: Open the entry you just saved. The details page presents the main text and "notes" separately, and the source area clearly displays source information; clicking on a valid web link can jump directly back to the original source in the browser.
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_058: Check that the text is not mixed with your own additions, that the notes explain what to do next time, and that source titles and links point to the same material. If the excerpts come from multiple pages, it is easier to retain the source by creating separate entries, and then export them together.

blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_060: The details page displays the saved exercise text, notes and source links.
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_061: 5. If you need to add something, return to the editing page
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_062: Click "Edit" on the details page to modify existing text, notes or sources, and click "Save" when finished. Existing notes and sources will be expanded on the editing page, making it easier to add analysis and conclusions.
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_063: In this example, you can retain "Friday review" as a fixed search term, and then add specific inspection results. Open the original link to verify before modifying the source. Do not fill in unverified information just to make the entry appear complete.

blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_065: Reopen the edit page of the same content, and the previously filled information will still be retained.
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_066: 6. Retrieve this clip using the words in the note
blog_guide-clipping-sources.text_067: Return to the Clips list and enter "Friday Review" in the search box at the top. Even if there are no these words in the text, the system will present the entry through the note content index.

blog_guide-guitar.text_036: Start by strumming one chord, then learn to move to the next one when the time is right. NinoPad puts six inductive strings and chord rockers on your mobile phone, and also provides a learning desktop. blog_guide-guitar.text_041: Practice with the default scheme first, turn down the volume, and confirm that the sound is playing from the intended speakers or headphones.
blog_guide-guitar.text_042: No need to connect to a Mac to play and learn locally; lessons use standard tunings and fixed fingerings.
blog_guide-guitar.text_043: 1. Strum the strings first and hear the current chord clearly.
blog_guide-guitar.text_044: Once on the guitar tabletop, lightly sweep across the six strings. You can tap on each string one by one, or you can strum multiple strings in succession; start slowly and make sure that each touch has a corresponding sound.
blog_guide-guitar.text_045: The direction of the strings can be adjusted. Regardless of whether it is arranged horizontally or vertically, swipe in the direction that can cross each string in turn. There is no need to copy the gesture direction on the screenshot. The small screen above displays the currently selected chord.

blog_guide-guitar.text_047: Real guitar controls are now operational, and strumming uses the phone's local sound source.
blog_guide-guitar.text_048: 2. Change the chords and try strumming again
blog_guide-guitar.text_049: Use the eight-way rocker to select another direction, first look at the chord name on the small screen, and then strum the strings. First divide "chord selection" and "strumming" into two actions, and then connect them together after you are familiar with them.
blog_guide-guitar.text_050: Use the mute key when you want to stop the sound immediately; the bend bar is used to change the pitch when the sound is made, and it will return to the center when you release it. There is no need to operate these controls simultaneously the first time, start by switching between the two chords steadily.
blog_guide-guitar.text_051: 3. Understand sounds and solutions from the console
blog_guide-guitar.text_052: Click "Control" and you can see the entrances of "Sound", "Performance", "Chords" and "Plan". First understand the current sound from the sound page, and then check your own chords and plans to avoid thinking of tuning and changing chords as the same thing.
blog_guide-guitar.text_053: Modifications in the console are saved to the current scenario. If you want to keep the original configuration, make a copy on the plan page and try again. After clicking "Finish" to return to the playing desktop, use the same chord to compare the sound before and after the adjustment.

blog_guide-guitar.text_055: Guitar consoles are grouped by sounds, performances, chords, and schemes.

blog_guide-guitar.text_057: Enter "Learning" in the desktop switch bar at the bottom, and click on the small screen above to open the song selection page. You can search by title or practice technique, or filter by style and difficulty; the full list has 100 exercises.
blog_guide-guitar.text_058: This time, enter "Jasmine" in the search box and click on the search result. The contents of the music library are independently arranged and simplified short harmony exercises, not original recordings or complete song scores. Choose a name that you are familiar with first to help you remember the chord changes you want to practice.
blog_guide-guitar.attr_059: The learning song selection page provides search, style and difficulty filters.
blog_guide-guitar.text_060: The learning song selection page provides search, style and difficulty filters.
blog_guide-guitar.text_061: 5. Listen to the demonstration first and observe the changes in prompts
blog_guide-guitar.text_062: After selecting the song, return to the learning desktop, keep the "Demonstration" mode first, and click play. Observe the chords, bars, and progressions on the small screen, and then pay attention to the prompts on the strings and joysticks. If you want to watch a section again, you can pause and adjust the progress.
blog_guide-guitar.text_063: Listen to a complete round for the first time, don't rush to catch up on all the prompts. Learn to use the course's own tunings and fingerings. The capo, transposition, or custom open strings you set in the playing plan will not be directly applied.
blog_guide-guitar.attr_064: Start the demonstration after selecting Jasmine, and the learning desktop displays the current chord and playing position.
blog_guide-guitar.text_065: Start the demonstration after selecting Jasmine, and the learning desktop displays the current chord and playing position.
blog_guide-guitar.text_066: 6. Cut to follow step by step and complete the movements slowly
blog_guide-guitar.text_067: After pausing the demonstration, switch the mode to "Follow Practice" and start practicing step by step. Follow the current chord and string position prompts and complete the current action correctly before proceeding to the next step. A strum will only advance the step corresponding to the first touch, and the entire exercise will not be skipped just because you drag through multiple strings.
blog_guide-guitar.text_068: If you encounter unfamiliar finger shapes, you can click on the small screen or the console to view them; enter the practice settings when you need to slow down and set the loop. When finished, click Pause, then change the song or return to the playing table, so that you can easily know where to continue next time.
blog_guide-guitar.text_070: Why don't you use my capo when studying?
blog_guide-guitar.text_071: The course uses standard tuning and fixed finger patterns, making it easy to practice according to the prompts. Capos, transpositions, and custom tunings for strumming plans do not directly override lessons.
blog_guide-guitar.text_072: The console does not turn on when strumming. Is it malfunctioning?
blog_guide-guitar.text_073: This prevents accidental opening of the console while the strings are in contact and for a short time after they are released. First let go and pause, then tap the console in place; starting to slide from the button may also be recognized as a strum gesture and cancel the opening.
blog_guide-guitar.text_074: Can lessons replace real guitar fingering practice?
blog_guide-guitar.text_075: The mobile phone mainly helps to understand the chord sequence, string position and rhythm. The fret strength, hand shape, and feel of a real guitar still require practice on the instrument.

blog_guide-synthesizer.text_036: There’s no need to cumbersomely connect a Mac or have a deep knowledge of arranging. Turn on the NinoPad synthesizer and tap a chord key to instantly play a beautiful melody. This tutorial will take you from listening to single-note chords to seamlessly switching to the arranger desktop to add drum beats. All steps can be listened to and debugged on the mobile phone in real time.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_037: The pictures are from the native app in the dedicated simulator, and are actually operated and screenshotted by the script. The connection state uses demo data; the local operation in this article does not require a Mac connection. Screenshots do not serve as verification of actual Mac MIDI output.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_040: Update to Milkcat Magic Control 1.3.0, turn on the sound and start practicing at a lower volume.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_041: Select "Synthesizer" from the "Layout" at the bottom and enter the "Chord" desktop first.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_042: This exercise uses the local high-quality sound source of the mobile phone; the Mac MIDI output can be configured as needed in subsequent connections.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_044: There are seven numbered chord keys clearly arranged on the chord desktop. The upper row is 2, 4, and 6, and the lower row is 1, 3, 5, and 7. Press and hold the 1 key first and then release it to listen to a clear and full attack and decay; then click the 4 or 5 keys in sequence to compare the auditory colors of different chord progressions.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_045: The small screen above displays the current key, chord names and performance status in real time. The numbers represent the steps in that key (for example, step 1 is not limited to C major). When you first start playing, it is recommended to keep the current key and focus on switching between different key positions. This will make it easier to establish an auditory perception of the changes in the series.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_047: Click the Sustain switch and press a chord key. Release your fingers at this time, and the chord sound will still continue melodiously, allowing you to free up your hands to adjust other knobs or switch desktops; the current picture shows the performance state after the sustain is turned on.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_048: After practice, click "Sustain" again to turn it off. If the sound continues, check to see if arranger or loop playback is also enabled. "Sustain" mainly controls the note continuation of a single chord, and the play key is responsible for scheduling the overall project rhythm.
blog_guide-synthesizer.attr_049: After the sustain is turned on, the small screen and chord keys retain the current performance status.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_050: After the sustain is turned on, the small screen and chord keys retain the current performance status.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_051: 3. Click the small screen to view the current performance settings
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_052: Click on the small screen above to bring up the detailed editing panel. The parameters in the panel will be dynamically adjusted according to the current desktop and performance mode; it is recommended to first observe the parameter partitions on the interface, fine-tune one knob at a time, and then return to the desktop to strike the same chord for listening comparison.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_053: After adjusting, click "Done" in the upper right corner to return. If you need to deeply customize the synthesizer tone, you can switch to the "Tone" desktop. Avoid making large-scale changes to multiple parameters at the same time before remembering the original sound, so that you can clearly feel the tuning effect of each knob.
blog_guide-synthesizer.attr_054: Click the small screen of the chord desktop to enter detailed editing. After completion, you can return to the original desktop.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_055: Click the small screen of the chord desktop to enter detailed editing. After completion, you can return to the original desktop.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_056: 4. Switch to the arrangement and generate a drum beat
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_057: Swipe the desktop switch bar at the bottom of the app to enter the "Arranger" desktop, or directly select it from the layout list. The four synthesizer desktops of chords, sounds, arrangements, and loops belong to the same project, so there is no need to recreate files.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_058: Click the "Variation" button to randomly generate a layered drum rhythm, and then click "Play". The step indicator light will jump with the beat, and the play button will switch to the stop state synchronously. It is recommended to listen to one or two measures in full to confirm the rhythm and charm before making adjustments to avoid confusion among multiple variations caused by rapid continuous taps.
blog_guide-synthesizer.attr_059: The drum beat variant has been generated on the arranger desktop and entered into the playback state.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_060: The drum beat variant has been generated on the arranger desktop and entered into the playback state.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_061: 5. Open the arranger editor and get to know different parts
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_062: During the playback process, you can observe the rhythm in real time; before in-depth fine-tuning, click Pause, then click the small screen above the arranger desktop to call out the editing page. The arranger editor divides the music content into independent pages for drum beats, chords, bass, melody and whole song structure. It is recommended to familiarize yourself with the percussion points of each step from the drum beats page.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_063: What is adjusted here is the voice sequence within the project. If you just want to change the sound quality of the instrument, it is more direct to go to the "Tone" desktop; if you need to record improvisation, you can go to the "Loop" desktop. First adjust one drum beat smoothly, and then gradually add other parts.
blog_guide-synthesizer.attr_064: Detailed editing of arrangements is paginated by part to avoid facing all parameters at once.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_065: Detailed editing of arrangements is paginated by part to avoid facing all parameters at once.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_067: Click "Finish" to return to the main desktop, confirm that the play button has returned to the waiting state, and turn off the sustain smoothly. This can clearly distinguish the actual effects of single note duration, timbre change and rhythm loop.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_068: Next, you can also explore the real-time recording, overdubbing and undoing functions of the loop desktop, or save and export the current project as a WAV audio or MIDI file for more operations. These operations will record your creative results. It is recommended to save the current practice draft before starting subsequent creation.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_070: There is no sound when pressing the keys, what should I check first?
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_071: Please first check the phone system volume and current audio output device, and confirm that you are not stuck in an error message or export pop-up window. There is no need to connect to a Mac to produce local sounds on your phone; if you choose external MIDI output, please check the local volume and the receiving channel of the external host software respectively.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_072: Is it another song after switching to other desktops?
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_073: No. The four desktops of the synthesizer control the same music project from different dimensions. Switching desktops does not create a new project, and there is no need to import sound materials repeatedly.
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_074: Can it be used directly as an instrument plug-in on Mac?
blog_guide-synthesizer.text_075: It can send MIDI control commands to the Mac, but the local sound source of the phone and the internal instruments of the Mac software belong to two independent channels. When you need your computer to produce sound, first connect your Mac, select a MIDI target, and configure the input mapping in the host DAW.

blog_guide-text-button.text_036: Why bother tapping the keyboard repeatedly when replying to fixed phrases, frequently used addresses or customer service templates several times a day? Create an exclusive text button in NinoPad, stop the cursor in the Mac window, and input accurately with just one tap on your phone. blog_guide-text-button.text_037: The images are from the app's native editor and content preview, using sample text and simulated connections. Preview only shows content on your phone; actual input and synchronization must be confirmed on a connected Mac.
blog_guide-text-button.text_040: Use Naimao Magic Control 1.2.0; enter the desktop with space to add buttons. This article starts with the work layout.
blog_guide-text-button.text_041: To actually use it on a computer, you need to connect to a computer running Naimao Magic Control for Mac, and follow the prompts to enable the required permissions for control.
blog_guide-text-button.text_042: First prepare a blank test document and place the cursor in the text to facilitate confirmation of the input position and the effect of additional keys.
blog_guide-text-button.text_043: 1. Add a shortcut button and select "Send Text"
blog_guide-text-button.text_044: Click "Layout" at the bottom, then click "Edit Current Desktop." After entering the editor, click "Add Component" and select the "Button" component; new buttons need to be configured first.
blog_guide-text-button.text_045: Click "Send Text" in "Common Operations" in the operation list, and the editing page with the same name will open. If you are adjusting an existing button, go to its "Action" page, click "Replace" next to the current operation, and then select "Send Text". Complete the content settings first, then adjust the button appearance.
blog_guide-text-button.text_047: Illustration of the editing entrance of work layout
blog_guide-text-button.text_048: 2. Save a complete and usable reply first
blog_guide-text-button.text_049: Fill in the "Enter text to send" field with practice sentences. Check the punctuation and wording, and leave the specific date, amount, or name that needs to be modified each time for actual use to avoid mistaking a certain reply as a general template.
blog_guide-text-button.text_050: Scroll down to "Save Name" and change the name to "Confirm Received". This name is used to identify the automation content; the text on the button surface is adjusted in the "Name" of the component "Appearance", and both need to be checked separately.
blog_guide-text-button.attr_051: The actual entered reply text; the save name and button appearance text are set separately.
blog_guide-text-button.text_052: The actual entered reply text; the save name and button appearance text are set separately.
blog_guide-text-button.text_053: 3. Decide whether to add keys after input is completed
blog_guide-text-button.text_054: Open "After completing input" in the "After input" area, you can select "Don't append keys", "Press Enter", "Press ⌘Enter" or customize shortcut keys. For the first exercise, select "Don't add keys" to let the text stay in the current input box, leaving an opportunity for inspection and modification.
blog_guide-text-button.text_055: Enter has different meanings in different software: it may be a new line or it may be sent directly. Only after the behavior has been confirmed in the target software, the corresponding button will be added to this reply. blog_guide-text-button.text_057: The "After typing" menu displays the available append key options. Practice keeping "No additional keys" first.
blog_guide-text-button.text_058: 4. Leave "Send once" and check with content preview
blog_guide-text-button.text_059: Leave "Send once" in "Send by". This example only has one text, no need to repeat rounds or hold down bursts. Click down on "Preview content" and check whether the sentence is fully displayed in the preview.
blog_guide-text-button.text_060: "Content Preview" only displays the content that will be taken out in this round. It will not operate the Mac, nor will it advance the progress of retrieving the official text list. You can click "Preview Next Round" to check again; seeing the text does not mean that the computer has received the text.
blog_guide-text-button.attr_061: The content preview actually displays the practice sentences and can be checked repeatedly. The preview itself does not operate the Mac.
blog_guide-text-button.text_062: The content preview actually displays the practice sentences and can be checked repeatedly. The preview itself does not operate the Mac.
blog_guide-text-button.text_063: 5. Save the configuration and verify it again in the Mac document
blog_guide-text-button.text_064: Close the content preview and return to the editing page. When an available automation service is connected, "Save and Sync" is displayed in the upper right corner; when not connected, "Save Draft" is displayed. Press the current button to save and watch if the page reports a sync failure or timeout.
blog_guide-text-button.text_065: Return to the component properties and click "Finish", then exit desktop editing. Now switch to the Mac test document, click the text to make the insertion cursor appear, and then click the new button on the phone. Only one reply should be inserted; there is no append key in this example and the text should remain in the document. If "To be synchronized" is still displayed, reconnect and open the edit page to save the synchronization and try again.
blog_guide-text-button.text_066: 6. When multiple replies are needed, expand the text list
blog_guide-text-button.text_067: Go back to "Edit text and send method", click "Add one" to continue writing the second one; if you already have line-by-line text, you can use "Import by line...", and each non-blank line in the import preview will become an independent entry.
blog_guide-text-button.text_068: "Access method" will appear in multiple texts. "Next in order" is used to retrieve items one by one, "Random one" and "Get in order after shuffling" are suitable for rotating materials, and "Enter all at once" will retrieve the entire list. blog_guide-text-button.text_071: Text input depends on the current input position of your Mac. blog_guide-text-button.text_072: The save name has been changed, but why hasn’t the word on the button changed?
blog_guide-text-button.text_073: Saving a name is a text action. Go back to the "Appearance" page of the component properties to modify the button display text, and then exit the editor to check.

blog_layout-arcade.text_036: Want to play some relaxing party games with friends? Open the built-in game lobby on the Mac, pair your phone and enter "Games" in the bottom layout, which can be used as a touch screen controller to control direction and movement. Games such as "Breaking Sky" and "Paper Soccer" support multiple mobile phones to join. blog_layout-arcade.text_037: Illustration showing the P1 controller, game menu, and landscape arrangement for a soccer example session. Real game response and multiple phones joining needs to be checked on the same paired Mac.
blog_layout-arcade.text_040: Install Naimao Control on iPhone/iPad, and install the companion client on Mac; complete the pairing, and allow accessibility permissions on the Mac client. When you need the computer screen, turn on the screen recording permission.
blog_layout-arcade.text_041: You need to have the arcade game installed and running on your Mac. The number of people and input method are determined by game adaptation; setting more people will not automatically change the single-player game to a multi-player game.
blog_layout-arcade.text_042: 1. Open the game lobby on Mac
blog_layout-arcade.text_043: Open NinoPad on Mac and directly enter the game lobby built into the client. You can browse supported party games such as "Breaking Sky" and "Paper Soccer" in the lobby, or you can try single-player projects first.
blog_layout-arcade.text_045: 2. Pair your phone and enter the game layout
blog_layout-arcade.text_046: Make sure your phone and Mac are paired successfully, tap "Layout" at the bottom of the phone app and switch to "Games." Confirm the player's seat according to the selected game, and the screen will automatically display the corresponding direction and action buttons.
blog_layout-arcade.text_047: After the phone and Mac are paired and switched to the game layout, select the game card in the Mac's built-in game lobby and start it. After confirming that the game screen appears on the Mac screen, check the player number displayed on the mobile phone and start playing with the touch screen controller.
blog_layout-arcade.text_048: 3. Claim the player number and test the response of the cross keys and action keys
blog_layout-arcade.text_049: After the game is started, check the player identification (such as P1) on the top of the phone. The small screen in the middle will display the name and running status of the currently running game.
blog_layout-arcade.text_050: Gently push the left cross direction key to control the movement of the character, tap the A, B, X, Y action keys on the right to verify the response to operations such as jumping and attacking, and confirm that the handle has been correctly bound to the current player seat. The key mapping for different games is subject to the current game settings.

blog_layout-arcade.text_052: P1 native handles and action tags in the football demo session.
blog_layout-arcade.text_053: 4. Tap the small LED screen in the middle to call up the main control management menu
blog_layout-arcade.text_054: During the game, tap the small LED screen in the middle of the phone. The master controller (P1) will see management operations such as "pause game", "return to game lobby" and "exit game".
blog_layout-arcade.text_055: When you need to pause, explicitly select "Pause Game" and confirm on your Mac screen that the game screen has stabilized. Calling out the menu itself does not mean that the game automatically pauses. When resuming play, just re-enter the menu and select continue.
blog_layout-arcade.attr_056: Click on the small screen to open the main control menu. From here, choose to pause, return to the lobby, or exit.
blog_layout-arcade.text_057: Click on the small screen to open the main control menu. From here, choose to pause, return to the lobby, or exit.
blog_layout-arcade.text_058: 5. Place the phone horizontally to experience the full-function shoulder key layout for both hands
blog_layout-arcade.text_059: Turn the phone sideways and check the location of the direction area, action keys and shoulder buttons. First release all the buttons, then change the holding method; do a slight direction input again to confirm the character's response.
blog_layout-arcade.text_060: The horizontal screen in the picture is the actual rotated App layout, not another game or another set of mapping.

blog_layout-arcade.text_062: The actual rotated horizontal handle follows the same football demo session.
blog_layout-arcade.text_063: 6. Connect to the second device for two-player battle, and exit safely at the end
blog_layout-arcade.text_064: After the second phone is paired with the same Mac, check to see if it gets another player ID, and then test independent movement separately. When waiting is displayed, check the game player limit and seats first, and do not start a new game repeatedly.
blog_layout-arcade.text_065: When it is time to end the game, the P1 controller selects to return to the lobby or exit the game in the small screen menu on the mobile phone. After confirmation on the Mac, the current game can be ended.
blog_layout-arcade.text_068: The game may only have one player seat, or it may be full. Check the number of people the game supports and the current player list; changing the number of people settings will not add multiplayer logic to the game.
blog_layout-arcade.text_069: Ordinary players click on a small screen and have no main control menu?
blog_layout-arcade.text_070: Pause, return to lobby and exit are provided by the master. First confirm whether the mobile phone displays the main controller or the identity of other players.
blog_layout-arcade.text_071: Can I directly use this layout to control any native Mac game?
blog_layout-arcade.text_072: The functions of this touch screen controller are subject to the Magic Control Game Hall and adapted games, and are not equivalent to universal system controllers.
