blog_layout-browser.text_036: When checking information and comparing information, frequent switching between the keyboard and mouse often interrupts the train of thought. The browser layout integrates direct URL access, multi-tab switching, and in-page search on the mobile phone screen. You can switch pages with a simple swipe, and even supports automatically calling up the specified browser when switching layouts.
blog_layout-browser.text_037: The accompanying picture demonstrates the URL input and browser settings on the mobile phone, and the Mac connection uses sample data. Whether the URL is opened and tabs are switched, please confirm in the paired Mac browser.
blog_layout-browser.text_040: Install Naimao Control 1.2.0 on iPhone/iPad, and install the companion version of the same version on Mac; complete the pairing, and allow accessibility permissions on the Mac side. When you need the computer screen, turn on the screen recording permission.
blog_layout-browser.text_041: Prepare a browser window on your Mac. The following explanation is based on the default shortcut keys; if you have modified the browser shortcut keys, restore or compare your own settings first.
blog_layout-browser.text_042: 1. Enter the browser layout and invoke the default browser
blog_layout-browser.text_043: Click the "Layouts" tab at the bottom of your iPhone, find and enter the "Browser" layout in the list. When there are many list items, you can quickly search through the search box at the top.
blog_layout-browser.text_044: After entering the layout, the App will automatically bring up the Mac's default browser to the foreground according to the preset action; you can also click the "Launch Browser" button on your phone at any time to actively send an activation request. The Mac default browser is taken from the macOS system settings.
blog_layout-browser.attr_045: The browser desktop includes URL input, new tab, in-page search, and tab controls.
blog_layout-browser.text_046: The browser desktop includes URL input, new tab, in-page search, and tab controls.
blog_layout-browser.text_047: 2. Enter and reach the target URL directly with one click
blog_layout-browser.text_048: Click "Enter URL or Search" on your phone and enter the target test URL in the pop-up text input panel, such as https://ninopad.com. After checking that everything is correct, click "Up Screen".
blog_layout-browser.text_049: The key has a coherent sequence of automated actions built into it: it automatically focuses the Mac browser's address bar, then fills in the full URL, and finally automatically sends Enter. Confirm on your Mac screen that the web page has started loading without having to manually hit Enter repeatedly at the end of the text.
blog_layout-browser.attr_050: The text input panel that opens after clicking "Enter URL or Search"; you can check the complete URL before sending.
blog_layout-browser.text_051: The text input panel that opens after clicking "Enter URL or Search"; you can check the complete URL before sending.
blog_layout-browser.text_052: 3. Create a new tab and experience the switching and closing of the slider.
blog_layout-browser.text_053: Click "New Tab" on your phone, confirm that a new blank tab has been created in the Mac browser, and then use the method in the previous step to open another reference webpage. Swipe the Tabs slider on your phone left or right and watch the Mac browser smoothly switch between adjacent tabs.
blog_layout-browser.text_054: Tap the slider control to quickly refresh the current page. Long pressing will trigger the closing of the current tab. If the closed page contains unsaved form data, please confirm the system pop-up prompt on the Mac before proceeding. If you close it by mistake, you can click "Restore Tab" to retrieve it again.
blog_layout-browser.text_055: 4. Quickly locate keywords in the text of the page
blog_layout-browser.text_056: Click the "Search on page" button on your phone, and the Mac browser will automatically bring up the text search bar (⌘F). Then click "Keyboard Input" and enter the words that actually exist on the current web page (such as "layout").
blog_layout-browser.text_057: Observe matching keyword highlighting positioning feedback on your Mac screen. This operation is used to quickly locate specific information on the current page; if you need to search the entire network, please return to "Enter URL or search" and enter the search term directly.
blog_layout-browser.text_058: 5. Check and configure the linkage actions after entering the layout
blog_layout-browser.text_059: Click "Layout" in the bottom bar to enter solution management, expand the menu next to the browser solution and select "Post-switch action". The panel provides modes such as "Don't execute", "Default browser" and "Specified App".
blog_layout-browser.text_060: First select "Default Browser" and save it to experience the linkage effect of automatically opening or activating the default browser on Mac every time you switch to this layout.
blog_layout-browser.attr_061: The "Post-switch action" settings page of the browser plan.
blog_layout-browser.text_062: The "Post-switch action" settings page of the browser plan.
blog_layout-browser.text_064: If you are more accustomed to using a specific third-party browser (such as Chrome, Edge, or Arc) for your daily work, you can select "Specify App" in "Post-Switch Action" and click the target software from the Mac application list.
blog_layout-browser.text_065: After saving the configuration, re-enter the browser layout and verify on the Mac whether the specified browser window is accurately opened. This setting only changes the startup target and does not change the browser's general shortcut key mapping rules.
blog_layout-browser.attr_066: Select "Specify App" to enter the form for manually specifying an app.
blog_layout-browser.text_067: Select "Specify App" to enter the form for manually specifying an app.
blog_layout-browser.text_069: The address is correct, why was it entered into the web form?
blog_layout-browser.text_070: Check whether the browser is in the foreground and whether the address bar focus shortcut Command-L has been modified or blocked. First manually confirm on your Mac that Command-L can enter the address bar, and then try again.
blog_layout-browser.text_071: History or tab shortcuts different from my browser?
blog_layout-browser.text_072: Presets rely on browser shortcuts. Different browsers and user-defined mappings may differ; check the corresponding button bindings through the layout editor.

blog_layout-codex.text_036: The original "Ambience Programming" has been renamed "Codex". This time, a separate "Ambience Programming" layout has been added for Mac local assistants such as Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity. The following will first explain how to choose between the two, and the original Codex operation tutorial will continue to be retained.
blog_layout-codex.text_038: New atmosphere programming, where to start?
blog_layout-codex.text_039: First update your phone and Mac companion to 1.3.1 and complete pairing on the same LAN. The corresponding programming assistant needs to be installed and logged in on the Mac first. The phone will not run the AI ​​model independently, and NinoPad Pro does not include third-party AI subscriptions.
blog_layout-codex.text_040: Select "Ambience Programming" in "Layout" at the bottom. There are "Project", "Session", "Queue" and "Settings" buttons at the bottom of the main interface.
blog_layout-codex.text_041: Select the project you want to continue through "Project" and view the session through "Session"; after an existing session is assigned to a button, click the corresponding button to switch. The small screen at the top displays the responses for the selected task.
blog_layout-codex.text_042: Switch between "Work", "Deliverables", "Documents", "Projects" and "Usage" on the small screen to view the information of the current session as needed. If you need to read a long reply, click "Expand". New commands are initiated from "New Task", and waiting tasks are viewed in the "Queue"; permission requests must first check the content before deciding whether to allow it.
blog_layout-codex.attr_043: The actual main interface of Atmosphere Programming displays the simulated conversation and replies of the travel wallet
blog_layout-codex.text_044: The real App main interface, items and responses are screenshots using simulated data. The available assistants, models, usage and operation options are subject to the actual installation and login status of the Mac.
blog_layout-codex.text_045: If you mainly want to view the six slots, quotas and reasoning levels of the Codex desktop task, select "Codex" and continue the following operations. If you need to run a local shell, use a separate "Terminal" layout.
blog_layout-codex.text_046: When letting AI write code, running multiple tasks at the same time often requires frequent screen switching to keep track of the progress. Codex layout provides you with a handheld scheduling platform: you can intuitively grasp the progress of each slot task on your mobile phone, click to view the status readback, double-click to focus the corresponding window on the front desk, and smoothly adjust the model inference intensity and usage readback, making multi-workflow scheduling easy.
blog_layout-codex.text_047: The tasks, models and quotas in the accompanying pictures use sample data, and the keyboard and settings page are from the actual app. Please check your tasks before practicing. Model options and quotas are subject to the actual account.
blog_layout-codex.text_050: Install Naimao Control on iPhone/iPad, and install the corresponding companion terminal on Mac; complete LAN pairing, and allow accessibility permissions on the Mac terminal. When you need the computer screen, turn on the screen recording permission.
blog_layout-codex.text_051: The Codex Desktop App needs to be pre-installed and logged in on your Mac, and have an active programming task. This layout is for task scheduling of Codex on Mac desktop; please use the terminal layout for command line sessions.
blog_layout-codex.text_052: 1. Enter the Codex layout and view the task slots
blog_layout-codex.text_053: Click the "Layouts" tab at the bottom of your iPhone, find and enter the "Codex" layout in the list. For multi-desktop solutions, please expand the arrow on the right and select the corresponding desktop.
blog_layout-codex.text_054: There are multiple task slot buttons displayed on the desktop, and the small screen at the top can read back the status of the currently selected task. If the task button is blank, please first confirm that the corresponding Codex/Agent development environment on the Mac is running and connected.
blog_layout-codex.text_055: The task button displays the current active slot, which facilitates intuitive management of multiple concurrent workflows. It does not mean that the account can only handle a limited number of tasks.
blog_layout-codex.attr_056: Codex desktop, task name, status and quota are all demonstration data.
blog_layout-codex.text_057: Codex desktop, task name, status and quota are all demonstration data.
blog_layout-codex.text_058: 2. Master the logic of single-click switching and double-clicking the foreground focus
blog_layout-codex.text_059: Under the default settings, clicking the task key will select the task in the background on the mobile phone, making it easy to view its context and status; double-clicking the task key will automatically bring the corresponding window activation on the Mac to the foreground while switching.
blog_layout-codex.text_060: Open multiple windows on Mac, try single-click and double-click operations respectively, observe the switching effect of the foreground focus, and ensure that tasks can be scheduled freely without disturbing the current writing idea.
blog_layout-codex.text_061: 3. Open the real-time keyboard, confirm the cursor position and enter the command
blog_layout-codex.text_062: After selecting the target task, click "Live Keyboard" on your phone and switch to "Live" input mode at the top (make sure it is not local draft mode).
blog_layout-codex.text_063: First confirm on the Mac that the cursor is in the Prompt input box of the target task, then enter the prepared command content on the mobile keyboard, and verify that the text input is completely correct on the Mac before sending.
blog_layout-codex.attr_064: The actual live keyboard opened from the Codex desktop; no input was made to the real task this time.
blog_layout-codex.text_065: The actual live keyboard opened from the Codex desktop; no input was made to the real task this time.
blog_layout-codex.text_066: 4. Adjust the model selection and inference strength knobs
blog_layout-codex.text_067: Return to the main Codex desktop and view the status readback under the "Model" and "Inference Strength" knobs. If you need to adjust the inference intensity, gently dial one gear at a time and wait for the current task parameters on the phone and Mac to be synchronized.
blog_layout-codex.text_068: The available models and inference levels depend on the specific services and account permissions you have bound. The quota panel provides a visual consumption reference to help you plan your token budget reasonably.
blog_layout-codex.text_069: 5. Enter the settings page and customize window focusing habits
blog_layout-codex.text_070: Click "Settings" in the bottom bar to enter the "Codex" detailed settings page. Here you can check the Agent service source and turn on or off "Focus on ChatGPT when clicked" and task completion event notifications according to personal operating habits.
blog_layout-codex.text_071: After the configuration is completed, return to the desktop and flexibly manage background tasks as needed. If you want to keep background processing silent, just keep clicking and unfocused.

blog_layout-creative.text_036: When creating 3D, your hands are often busy moving back and forth between shortcut keys and the mouse wheel. The application creation platform will dynamically transform according to the current front-end software: just tap in Blender to focus on objects, switch editing modes or surround the viewing angle, and hold it horizontally to enjoy efficient blind operations brought by ergonomics.
blog_layout-creative.text_037: The illustrations use the Blender sample working state, and the horizontal and vertical screens and editing portal are operated within the app. The modeling exercise is written based on the current adaptation mapping. Please confirm the effect item by item in your own Blender temporary scene.
blog_layout-creative.text_040: Install Naimao Control 1.2.0 on iPhone/iPad, and install the companion version of the same version on Mac; complete the pairing, and allow accessibility permissions on the Mac side. When you need the computer screen, turn on the screen recording permission.
blog_layout-creative.text_041: Open Blender on your Mac, use the default shortcut configuration and a temporary scene, and place your mouse over the 3D view. Customized key positions, focus on the text box, and inputting transformation values ​​may all change the effect of shortcut keys.
blog_layout-creative.text_042: 1. Start Blender on Mac and enter the application creation platform
blog_layout-creative.text_043: Launch Blender on your Mac and open a 3D practice project. Click "Layout" at the bottom of your iPhone, find and enter the "App Creation Station" layout in the list.
blog_layout-creative.text_044: Observe the software status bar at the top of the phone to confirm that the foreground application has been accurately identified as "Blender", and the buttons below automatically appear as 3D view-specific controls such as "Focus Selected", "Select All", and "Deselect". "Desktop Objects.blend" in the screenshot is the name of the sample project and no additional download is required.
blog_layout-creative.text_045: If the keys of other software are still displayed on the mobile phone, click the Blender window on the Mac to bring it to the foreground to automatically refresh the status to avoid accidentally touching keys under incorrect mapping.

blog_layout-creative.text_047: The application creation platform in Blender demo state, the control name corresponds to the modeling scene.
blog_layout-creative.text_048: 2. Use all selection and deselection to verify the two-way linkage of the viewport
blog_layout-creative.text_049: In Blender's 3D viewport, first click the "Select All" button on your phone to see if all objects in the Mac scene are highlighted; then click "Deselect" to confirm that the selection is completely cleared.
blog_layout-creative.text_050: These two basic operations can help determine whether the focus accurately stays in the 3D viewport. If you were editing the text attribute box before, please exit the text input and move the mouse back to the 3D viewport before verifying.
blog_layout-creative.text_051: 3. Select the model mesh and test "focus selected" and perspective surround
blog_layout-creative.text_052: Select an object directly in Blender, then click "Focus Selected" on your phone to check whether the view adjusts around the selected object. Then gently adjust the horizontal and vertical surround controls and observe the change in viewing angle.
blog_layout-creative.text_053: Perspective changes are not the same as object transformations. Orbiting is the viewing direction; "Move", "Rotate" and "Scale" on the direction control will enter the object transformation operation and should not be mixed continuously without distinguishing them.
blog_layout-creative.text_054: 4. Switch to editing mode to safely perform modeling adjustments
blog_layout-creative.text_055: After selecting the editable object, click the "Switch Mode" button to check the current mode of Blender; press it again to return. The same shortcut key may act on objects, vertices, or other elements when in different modes.
blog_layout-creative.text_056: Complete the selection and pattern exercises before using delete or transform. If you need to cancel the ongoing Blender operation, first press Escape on your Mac to confirm that it has returned to a stable state.
blog_layout-creative.text_057: 5. Place the phone horizontally to experience the wide-width two-hand control engineering
blog_layout-creative.text_058: Place the phone horizontally and the interface will automatically rearrange into a horizontal screen wide creation platform. Hold it naturally with both hands, re-confirm the positions of the main knobs and function keys, and enjoy an ergonomic and fast blind operation experience.
blog_layout-creative.text_059: Horizontal screen adaptation only reorganizes the UI layout and does not change Blender's project status or mode settings. You can still view the current object and viewport rendering in real time on the Mac screen.

blog_layout-creative.text_063: Click "Layout → Edit Current Desktop" to freely adjust the position and mapping binding of existing components according to your personal workflow. It is recommended to note down the original functions before modification, and verify them by testing each button after completion.
blog_layout-creative.text_064: When switching to editing, drawing or audio software, the sub-console will be reloaded according to the corresponding configuration. blog_layout-creative.text_071: First check the front-end application, editing context and supporting integration status. The control should be enabled only if the adapter provides the corresponding capabilities; functions not provided by the software cannot be obtained by forcing the button to light up.
blog_layout-creative.text_072: My Blender operations are different from the tutorial?
blog_layout-creative.text_073: Check default key bindings, 3D view focus, and object/edit mode before verifying the operation directly on your Mac. Imported custom presets retain their own bindings and are not guaranteed to be the same as the built-in schemes.

Financial layout integrates an independent local calculator, and can also help you set up complex SUMIFS summary formulas through the visual panel, and copy or send them to the table with one click, making tedious data entry organized.
blog_layout-finance.text_037: Calculating 0.1+0.2, filling in SUMIFS parameters and copying formulas are all completed within the app. The screenshot uses the example connection; the final step requires validating the formula calculation in your spreadsheet software.

blog_layout-finance.text_041: Local computing and copying can be performed without a Mac. To send to a form, first prepare a blank worksheet and enter 1, 0, 2 in A1:A3 and 10, 20, 30 in C1:C3, leaving other relevant rows blank.
blog_layout-finance.text_042: 1. Enter the financial "entry" desktop and use the local calculator
blog_layout-finance.text_043: Click "Layouts" at the bottom of your iPhone, find and enter the "Finance" layout in the list. After expanding the plan, enter the "Entry" desktop and switch to "Calculator" on the bottom mode bar.
blog_layout-finance.text_044: Press AC to clear the old value, click 0, ., 1, +, 0, ., 2, = in sequence, and the result 0.3 is calculated on the small screen. The numeric keyboard and calculator remain independent, and switching modes will not interfere with current input on your Mac.

blog_layout-finance.text_048: Click "Copy" on the right side of the calculator. Your phone will prompt "Copied" and the calculation results have been entered into your phone's clipboard. Open Excel or Numbers on your Mac and select a blank test cell.
blog_layout-finance.text_049: Then click the "Send" button on the phone to inject the value directly into the cell, and finally press the Enter key on the Mac form to complete the entry. "Send" only sends numerical text and will not automatically submit a carriage return, allowing you to easily check the location.
blog_layout-finance.text_050: 3. Switch to "Statistics Summary" and long press to call out the SUMIFS panel
blog_layout-finance.text_051: Click "Layout" in the bottom bar and switch to the "Statistical Summary" desktop in the financial plan. Find the "SUMIFS" function button, press it with your finger for about one second and then release it to bring up the formula parameter panel filled in item by item.

blog_layout-finance.text_057: In the parameter panel, fill in: summation area

blog_layout-finance.text_061: That’s it. The system will automatically wrap it in English double quotes. Do not manually enter the quotes again.
blog_layout-finance.text_065: Click "Close Keyboard" and carefully check the generated standard formula in the formula preview bar at the bottom
blog_layout-finance.text_066: , ensuring that the parameter order is consistent with the range.

blog_layout-finance.text_070: Click "Copy Formula" and after seeing "Copied", the formula has been entered into the phone clipboard. If there is no shared clipboard between the two ends, you can manually enter this formula on the Mac; you can also connect the Mac and select a blank cell like D1, click "Send Formula", and finally press Enter in the table.
blog_layout-finance.text_071: For the prepared three rows of practice data, if column A is greater than 0, rows 1 and 3 will be selected, and the corresponding values in column C will add up to 40. This 40 is the expected mathematical result for the exercise data; please do the actual calculation with your table to make sure the formula is recognized and not treated as normal text.
blog_layout-finance.text_072: 6. Add multi-dimensional conditions to adapt to regional language separators
blog_layout-finance.text_073: If you need to add multi-dimensional filtering conditions, click the "Add a set of conditions" button in the panel and add condition area 2 and condition 2 respectively. Before all new parameters are completed, the copy and send buttons will be in error-proofing state, and all range lines should be strictly aligned.
blog_layout-finance.text_074: If your Excel working environment uses semicolons to separate parameters, you can switch the separator to "semicolon;" in the panel navigation menu and preview again. After practicing, click the close button to return to the desktop. Once you are proficient, you can quickly enter prefixes with just a short press.
blog_layout-finance.text_077: The local calculator handles it as a continuous operation: first complete 2+3, then multiply by 4. It is not an expression editor with operation precedence; complex calculations should be completed in table formulas.

blog_layout-launcher.text_036: No need to rummage through the crowded Dock or Launchpad. The launcher layout turns high-frequency apps on the computer into clear and easy-to-recognize solid blocks on the phone, and you can go directly to the front desk with a tap of your fingertips. This article will help you start by adding Safari and master the layout and management skills of the handheld launcher.
blog_layout-launcher.text_037: The system application icon and sample application directory are used for illustrations, and the process of adding buttons is completed within the app. When your Mac is connected, the list of apps is based on what's available on that computer.
blog_layout-launcher.text_040: Install Naimao Control 1.2.0 on iPhone/iPad, and install the companion version of the same version on Mac; complete the pairing, and allow accessibility permissions on the Mac side. When you need the computer screen, turn on the screen recording permission.
blog_layout-launcher.text_041: Leave the Mac companion running and wait for your app list to sync. The screenshots only use the demo directories of system applications such as Finder, Safari, Notes, etc.; your list is subject to the actual installed software.
blog_layout-launcher.text_042: 1. Enter the launcher and check the application name first
blog_layout-launcher.text_043: Click "Layout" at the bottom of the app and find "Launcher" in the list. When there are many layouts, use the search box to search for the name; if there are multiple desktops, click the arrow on the right to expand it, and then click the desktop name; you can also find it by searching for the specific desktop name.
blog_layout-launcher.text_044: Each big button represents a Mac App. The icons in the screenshot are from system applications and are not blank placeholders. First select an app that you can confirm directly on your Mac, such as Safari; short-press to send a request to open or activate the app, and then observe the Mac front window.
blog_layout-launcher.attr_045: System application demo directory in the launcher; user devices synchronize their own application list.
blog_layout-launcher.text_046: System application demo directory in the launcher; user devices synchronize their own application list.
blog_layout-launcher.text_047: 2. Long press a button to enter editing
blog_layout-launcher.text_048: Press and hold the existing application button in the launcher for about one second. After letting go, you will enter the editor and select the button. Confirm that the "Change App" and Add App entries appear on the page before proceeding to the next step.
blog_layout-launcher.text_049: Short press to start, long press to edit. If the app is just opened, it means that the operation is recognized as a short press; just go back to the button and press it again.
blog_layout-launcher.attr_050: After long-pressing the existing app button, the editor displays the current selection and "Change App".
blog_layout-launcher.text_051: After long-pressing the existing app button, the editor displays the current selection and "Change App".
blog_layout-launcher.text_052: 3. Open the App list and search for the software you want to add.
blog_layout-launcher.text_053: Click "Add App" in the upper left corner of the editor and find "Search App" in the operation panel. Enter the software name and click the required App from the application list connected to Mac; check the name after selecting it, and then click "Finish" in the upper right corner of the panel.
blog_layout-launcher.text_054: Shown here is the app catalog provided by the connected Mac, not the App Store. If the search fails, first confirm that the software is indeed installed on that Mac, and then check whether the directory has been synchronized; do not just fill in a guessed application ID.
blog_layout-launcher.attr_055: The actual app picker that opens when adding an app to search for apps on your connected Mac.
blog_layout-launcher.text_056: The actual app picker that opens when adding an app to search for apps on your connected Mac.
blog_layout-launcher.text_057: 4. Finish editing and verify the new button on your Mac
blog_layout-launcher.text_058: After returning to the editor from the app selector, check the new button's name and icon, then click Done to exit the editor. Short-press the new button to confirm that your Mac opens the selected software.
blog_layout-launcher.text_059: If the button is outside the current screen, check other desktops under Scheme. Launcher defaults are grouped by up to eight app buttons per desktop; custom arrangements of existing desktops will also affect where you see them.
blog_layout-launcher.attr_060: Return to the launcher after actually selecting Safari and completing two levels of editing; Mac launch results still need to be checked on a real connection.
blog_layout-launcher.text_061: Return to the launcher after actually selecting Safari and completing two levels of editing; Mac launch results still need to be checked on a real connection.
blog_layout-launcher.text_062: 5. When replacement is needed, use “Replace App”
blog_layout-launcher.text_063: Press and hold the existing button again, click "Change App", and then select another software from the list. This is editing the target of the button, and adding a new button is two different operations.
blog_layout-launcher.text_064: "Manually specify app" is used when the exact Bundle ID is known, such as com.apple.finder. After filling in, you still need to short press to verify. Similar application names do not prove that the binding is correct.
blog_layout-launcher.text_066: Why is my launcher different from the app in the screenshot?
blog_layout-launcher.text_067: The first synchronization will use the Dock application information connected to the Mac, and you can edit it later. The demo directory is only used for screenshots and will not replace your real application directory.
blog_layout-launcher.text_068: I clicked the button but no new window appeared on my Mac?
blog_layout-launcher.text_069: Existing applications may only be activated, not necessarily create new windows. First check whether the Mac menu bar is switched to the application, and then check the installation status, connection status and button binding.

blog_layout-media.text_032: Reproduce the classic click wheel and hierarchical menu feel, check the current track and cover at any time, smoothly fine-tune the playback progress and switch playback modes.

blog_layout-media.text_036: When listening to music for work, you can switch songs and adjust the volume without interrupting your focused work on the screen. The media layout reproduces the classic virtual click wheel interaction with the small screen. You can precisely fine-tune the song progress by sliding, and you can explore the playback mode by tapping MENU, bringing a ritualistic music remote control experience.
blog_layout-media.text_037: The track "Afternoon Practice" in the accompanying picture is sample data, and the menu is from the actual App interface. For final results on playback, progress, and modes, please check against the Mac player you are using.
blog_layout-media.text_040: Install Naimao Control 1.2.0 on iPhone/iPad, and install the companion version of the same version on Mac; complete the pairing, and allow accessibility permissions on the Mac side. When you need the computer screen, turn on the screen recording permission.
blog_layout-media.text_041: Manually play a song you have permission to play in the Music app on Mac. Check whether the corresponding song name is displayed on your phone; the "Afternoon Practice" in the screenshot of this article is a fictitious demo entry, not the real track that needs to be searched.
blog_layout-media.text_042: 1. Enter the media layout and check the currently playing information
blog_layout-media.text_043: Click the "Layouts" tab at the bottom of your iPhone, find and enter the "Media" layout in the list. If there are many layouts, you can use the search bar at the top to quickly locate them.
blog_layout-media.text_044: After entering, first observe whether the song name, artist, playback progress and status displayed on the small screen of your mobile phone are consistent with the player running on your Mac. Press the play/pause key to confirm that the Mac sound is paused immediately, and press the key again to resume playback.
blog_layout-media.attr_045: The media desktop displays the demo track "Afternoon Practice", and no real player is connected this time.
blog_layout-media.text_046: The media desktop displays the demo track "Afternoon Practice", and no real player is connected this time.
blog_layout-media.text_047: 2. Press the MENU key to enter the small screen level menu
blog_layout-media.text_048: Click the MENU button above the roulette wheel, and the small screen of your phone will immediately switch from playback view to hierarchical menu mode. You can either click on the menu item directly on the screen, or slide the cursor along the virtual click wheel, and finally press the center confirmation key to enter the selected item.
blog_layout-media.text_049: First find "Now Playing". In other menu pages, MENU is used to return to the previous level; you can continue to view song information after returning to "Now Playing".
blog_layout-media.attr_050: After clicking MENU, the actual menu entry is displayed on the small screen.
blog_layout-media.text_051: After clicking MENU, the actual menu entry is displayed on the small screen.
blog_layout-media.text_052: 3. Configure playback mode and two-way status synchronization
blog_layout-media.text_053: Click "Play Mode" in the menu to view control options such as random play, single loop, list loop, etc. After selecting one of them, check whether the corresponding mode icon changes simultaneously in the Mac player interface.
blog_layout-media.text_054: The functions provided by different players (such as Apple Music and Spotify) are slightly different; for example, the function of collecting songs depends on the support of the specific player, and the interface options are subject to the actual playback ability.
blog_layout-media.attr_055: The actual play mode page that opens; options are determined by player capabilities.
blog_layout-media.text_056: The actual play mode page that opens; options are determined by player capabilities.
blog_layout-media.text_057: 4. Use the virtual scroll wheel to fine-tune progress
blog_layout-media.text_058: Return to the "Now Playing" interface and press the center confirmation key to enter the "Adjust Progress" mode. At this time, swipe the click wheel clockwise or counterclockwise to observe the changes in the time value on the small screen, and confirm on the Mac that the audio playback position has been accurately adjusted.
blog_layout-media.text_059: The center confirmation key can also rotate between views such as cover images and song details. Please read the page title clearly before operating the scroll wheel to avoid confusing volume adjustment with progress adjustment.
blog_layout-media.attr_060: "Adjust progress" status of the song page; first slide the click wheel slightly, then check the player position.
blog_layout-media.text_061: "Adjust progress" status of the song page; first slide the click wheel slightly, then check the player position.
blog_layout-media.text_062: 5. Return to daily playback to understand player permissions and restrictions.
blog_layout-media.text_063: After practicing, press the MENU key to return to the "Now Playing" main interface and retain the desired play mode. Functions such as playlist expansion, real-time lyrics display, and audio track output switching rely on the data channel opened by the Mac player to the system.
blog_layout-media.text_064: If a display is temporarily unavailable, first complete the same operation on your Mac to confirm that the player itself provides it. Just because a regular player can receive playback controls doesn't necessarily mean it can provide lyrics, collections, or a complete library.
blog_layout-media.text_066: Your phone has a play button but no song title?
blog_layout-media.text_067: Play a song on your Mac first, then check your media sources and connections. Ordinary media control and track information reading are different capabilities and are not guaranteed to be available at the same time.
blog_layout-media.text_068: What to do if the lyrics or playlist is empty?
blog_layout-media.text_069: Do not use repeated clicks to infer that the read has been successful. First check the player support and song information; if the lyrics do not match, you can try again later. If the database is empty, check the content on Mac.
blog_layout-media.text_070: This article is written based on the interface and operation of Naimao Magic Control 1.2.0, and was updated on September 10, 2026.

blog_layout-presentation.text_036: When giving a speech on stage or reporting remotely, the mobile phone is not only a flexible page turner, but also an all-round main control center. You can freely configure the position of the portrait camera and mobile phone screen projection window, and use the segmented timer that can be recorded to help you calmly control the rhythm of the entire presentation in every presentation.
blog_layout-presentation.text_037: Camera settings, screen casting settings and timers are all operated in the App and screenshots taken. Mac connection uses sample state; actual capture and casting needs to be started, checked, and ended on your device.
blog_layout-presentation.text_040: Install Naimao Control 1.2.0 on iPhone/iPad, and install the companion version of the same version on Mac; complete the pairing, and allow accessibility permissions on the Mac side. When you need the computer screen, turn on the screen recording permission.
blog_layout-presentation.text_041: Prepare a disposable presentation file. To use a camera or mobile phone to mirror the screen, follow the actual system prompts to grant the corresponding permissions; you only need to adjust the floating window settings without starting collection.
blog_layout-presentation.text_042: 1. Enter the lecture assistant desktop and verify remote page turning.
blog_layout-presentation.text_043: Click "Layout" at the bottom of the iPhone, expand the presentation plan and select the "Lecture Assistance" desktop. The desktop is neatly arranged with core control keys such as previous page, next page, iPhone camera, and mobile screen projection.
blog_layout-presentation.text_044: Open a Keynote or PowerPoint presentation on your Mac and enter full-screen mode. Click "Next Page" on your phone to confirm on the Mac screen that the slide has successfully advanced to the next slide; click "Previous Page" to go back.
blog_layout-presentation.attr_045: Lecture assistance desktop, camera and mobile screen projection button are adjacent.
blog_layout-presentation.text_046: Lecture assistance desktop, camera and mobile screen projection button are adjacent.
blog_layout-presentation.text_047: 2. Long press the camera button to customize the picture-in-picture floating window on Mac
blog_layout-presentation.text_048: Press and hold the iPhone Camera button for about a second and when you let go, you should be taken to Camera Settings. Click "Upper Left", and then drag the "Floating Window Size" slider; click "Round Corners" if you need rounded corners.
blog_layout-presentation.text_049: Check the position preview and size changes. The mirror image only affects the camera display direction. Whether to turn it on or not depends on the effect you want the audience to see. Set the completion point to "Done" and return to speech assistance.
blog_layout-presentation.attr_050: In the camera settings page that is actually entered by long pressing, the upper left corner and rounded corners have been selected and resized.
blog_layout-presentation.text_051: In the camera settings page that is actually entered by long pressing, the upper left corner and rounded corners have been selected and resized.
blog_layout-presentation.text_052: 3. Independently configure the position of the floating window for mobile screen projection
blog_layout-presentation.text_053: Long press the "Mobile Screen Mirroring" button to enter the independent screen mirroring floating window settings page. The mobile screen projection and camera floating windows have their own independent sizes and docking position settings, so they will not overlap or interfere with each other.
blog_layout-presentation.text_054: Select a corner of the screen (such as the lower right corner) that does not block the core text and chart data of the slide. After adjusting the size, click "Finish" to exit the settings.
blog_layout-presentation.attr_055: The actual screen mirroring settings page opened by long pressing is separate from the camera settings.
blog_layout-presentation.text_056: The actual screen mirroring settings page opened by long pressing is separate from the camera settings.
blog_layout-presentation.text_057: 4. Practical demonstration: turn on the camera and screen projection with one click
blog_layout-presentation.text_058: After adjustment, short press the camera entry to enter the camera process; short press the mobile screen projection entry to enter the screen casting process. After completing the startup according to the system interface, you must confirm on Mac that the screen appears, is in the appropriate position, and has the correct content.
blog_layout-presentation.text_059: Start by using a page without sensitive content. When finished, use the corresponding shutdown or system stop broadcast entry; returning to the settings page does not mean that the system broadcast has been stopped.
blog_layout-presentation.text_060: 5. Switch to speech timing and conduct segmented rhythm rehearsal
blog_layout-presentation.text_061: Click "Layout" in the bottom bar, search and switch to the "Speech Timing" desktop. Find the timer component and click "Start" at the beginning of the speech; whenever you finish a chapter or key point, tap "Pick" to record the time spent in each segment.
blog_layout-presentation.text_062: The "pointing" operation will leave a clear record of segment time and will not interrupt the overall total time at all; click "Pause" after the rehearsal to review the time distribution of each part. If you want to start a new round of rehearsal, click "Reset".
blog_layout-presentation.attr_063: The interface after actually starting the timer and setting the timer.
blog_layout-presentation.text_064: The interface after actually starting the timer and setting the timer.
blog_layout-presentation.text_065: 6. Complete the simulation throughout the entire process and confidently control the pace of the scene
blog_layout-presentation.text_066: Before officially going on stage, it is recommended to conduct a complete rehearsal according to the real process: open the screening, verify the front and rear page turning, call out the required portrait pop-up window, start the rehearsal timer and record it. Each step is verified with feedback on the Mac screen and mobile phone.
blog_layout-presentation.text_067: If you only need basic page turning for a certain speech, you can use the speech auxiliary desktop alone. There is no need to force the camera or screen projection function, and it will be more comfortable to travel lightly.
blog_layout-presentation.text_069: Why does long pressing directly open the camera?
blog_layout-presentation.text_070: Use long press for setting and short press for activation. Press and hold for about one second before letting go, and make sure the title you enter is "Camera Settings"; do not make an additional click after long pressing.
blog_layout-presentation.text_071: The timer changes but no screen appears on your Mac?
blog_layout-presentation.text_072: Timing and image capture are different functions. The timer running does not mean that the camera or screen mirroring has started. You still need to check the system acquisition status and the Mac receiving screen.

blog_layout-reading.text_036: When studying long PDFs or white papers on your computer, you can easily get lost by dragging the scroll bar frequently. blog_layout-reading.text_042: 1. Enter the reading layout and prepare the test document on Mac

blog_layout-reading.text_047: 2. Test single page flipping, confirm response and reader focus
blog_layout-reading.text_048: Click "Next Page" on the mobile reading desktop and observe whether the document in the Mac reader smoothly flips to the next page; then click "Previous Page" to return.
blog_layout-reading.text_049: Confirm that page turning shortcuts on your phone and Mac Reader are responding accurately with a single tap. In continuous scrolling mode, please refer to the actual field of view presented by the reader.
blog_layout-reading.text_050: 3. Read the chapter table of contents and check the document hierarchy
blog_layout-reading.text_051: Click the "Directory" button on your phone and wait for the phone to read and present the hierarchical directory list of the document. Check whether the chapter titles displayed in the list match the actual bookmarks of the Mac PDF.
blog_layout-reading.text_052: If the reader does not open the table of contents readback interface to the system, the interface will give friendly prompts; the demonstration chapter in this article is used to verify the table of contents interaction logic, and does not mean that all documents without bookmarks can automatically generate a table of contents.

blog_layout-reading.text_055: 4. Search for the chapter title and click to jump.
blog_layout-reading.text_056: Enter a chapter keyword (such as "Chapter 2") in the "Search Chapter" box at the top of the table of contents panel, and the list will filter out matching entries in real time.
blog_layout-reading.text_057: Click on the target chapter, the table of contents panel will automatically collapse, and the document on the Mac screen will immediately jump to the start page of the corresponding chapter. The pop-up window on the mobile phone closes to indicate that the command has been issued. Please confirm on the Mac that the page has been reached.
blog_layout-reading.attr_058: Filter results after actually entering "Chapter 2" on the contents page.
blog_layout-reading.text_059: Filter results after actually entering "Chapter 2" on the contents page.
blog_layout-reading.text_060: 5. Use "jump page number" to go directly to the specified page
blog_layout-reading.text_061: Click the "More" menu on the reading desktop and select "Jump Page Number". Enter the target page number (for example, 3) in the pop-up number box and click "Go".
blog_layout-reading.text_062: Check the current page number and text content of the document on Mac to confirm that the absolute page number jump is accurate. Note that the physical page number of the PDF file may include the cover page and the preface, and it is normal to have a slight deviation from the printed page number of the main text.
blog_layout-reading.attr_063: After entering document page number 3, the Go button becomes available; check the page content on Mac after the jump.
blog_layout-reading.text_064: After entering document page number 3, the Go button becomes available; check the page content on Mac after the jump.
blog_layout-reading.text_065: 6. Switch to text search and locate document details in depth

blog_layout-reading.text_067: If a purely scanned image PDF does not undergo OCR text layer recognition, it may not be possible to directly retrieve the text; when you encounter the essential paragraphs, you can use the clipboard function to organize and archive them.
blog_layout-reading.text_069: There is no directory. Is the app not connected?
blog_layout-reading.text_070: Not necessarily. The document may not have readable bookmarks, or the reader may not provide table of contents capabilities. Check page turning and text search first, and then check the table of contents of the document itself.
blog_layout-reading.text_071: Why doesn’t my phone display the entire PDF?
blog_layout-reading.text_072: This layout is the control interface for Mac Reader. It reads the available state and sends actions without automatically importing the entire book to the phone.

blog_layout-research.text_036: Reading and research are not just copying words, but also a process of pondering. The research layout allows you to capture exciting selections on the screen at any time, jot down personal insights on your phone and retain complete sources, so that every piece of information collected can be valuable in the future.
blog_layout-research.text_037: The selections and sources in the accompanying images are practice material. Adding new clips, filling in notes, saving and reopening are all done within the app; you can reproduce this process using the two sentences in the article.
blog_layout-research.text_040: Install Nanny Control 1.2.0 on your iPhone/iPad to practice manual clipping. When you need to read Mac text selections, install the same version of the Mac companion, complete pairing and allow accessibility permissions.
blog_layout-research.text_041: If you don't have a Mac, you can start directly from step 2 of adding clips manually. To practice the original text, use "Tutorial practice: first ask questions, then check the original text." This sentence is an operation example and is not used as an external reference.
blog_layout-research.text_042: 1. Select a piece of original text on Mac and then enter the survey
blog_layout-research.text_043: Select a small piece of text in a readable document or web page on your Mac and enter "Layout → Research" on your phone. Check whether the selection preview is consistent with what you just selected.
blog_layout-research.text_044: Check with short sentences first, don’t start with a full page screenshot. The source title and address will only appear if the system can read it; if the source is missing, manually check the original web page before saving.
blog_layout-research.attr_045: Selection and source preview of the research desktop; the picture shows the clear demonstration content.
blog_layout-research.text_046: Selection and source preview of the research desktop; the picture shows the clear demonstration content.
blog_layout-research.text_047: 2. Open the clipboard and add a new exercise text
blog_layout-research.text_048: Click "Clips" and then click the Add button. In the "Add text..." area, enter "Tutorial exercise: ask questions first, then check the original text." This is an operational exercise, not a citation from external literature.
blog_layout-research.text_049: The add page also provides album, file and paste entries. In this exercise, you only enter text. First, go through the saving and retrieval processes; then add attachments according to data type during formal collection.
blog_layout-research.text_050: 3. Expand "Notes" and write down your own understanding
blog_layout-research.text_051: Click the "Notes" folded area and scroll down to find the input box if necessary. Fill in "My notes: cite after adding the source." and make sure it goes into the notes area and is not followed by the original text.
blog_layout-research.text_052: If there is an authentic source, click "Source" and fill in the source title and link. This exercise has no external source, so keep it empty; check the two paragraphs of text and click "Save" in the upper right corner.
blog_layout-research.attr_053: Edit page after actually filling in the original text and expanding the note; the save button is now available.
blog_layout-research.text_054: Edit page after actually filling in the original text and expanding the note; the save button is now available.
blog_layout-research.text_055: 4. Find the content you just saved in the list
blog_layout-research.text_056: After saving, go back to the Clip List and find the entry that begins with "Tutorial Exercises." If there are many entries, enter the keyword in the search box to check whether you can find it.
blog_layout-research.text_057: This step is more reliable than just seeing the "Save" button disappear: the actual appearance of the content in the list means that it has been entered into the current clipboard.

blog_layout-research.text_071: Can I still organize my saved content without connecting to my Mac?

blog_layout-sampler.text_036: Capture sonic inspiration anytime, anywhere, without needing to connect to a computer. The sample layout has built-in sound libraries and responsive percussion pads that support volume fine-tuning, loudness optimization, and mutually exclusive group settings, allowing you to create dynamic beats at the tap of your fingertips.
blog_layout-sampler.text_037: Screenshot from the app's native sampler, using playable synthesized sample drum sounds. This time, actually click on the drum pad and open the sound editing page; screenshots cannot prove the listening experience of the speakers. Please confirm on your own device when listening.
blog_layout-sampler.text_040: Install Naimao Magic Control 1.2.0 on iPhone/iPad. You don't need a Mac for this exercise. Turn down the volume before starting to avoid hearing the sound the first time.
blog_layout-sampler.text_041: Use the built-in examples or audio you have access to. The kick, snare, hi-hat, and claps in the screenshots are synthesized samples, not user recordings.
blog_layout-sampler.text_042: 1. Load samples from the sound library
blog_layout-sampler.text_043: Click "Layout" at the bottom of the app and find "Sampling" in the list. When there are many layouts, use the search box to search for the name; if there are multiple desktops, click the arrow on the right to expand it, and then click the desktop name; you can also find it by searching for the specific desktop name. Enter the "Record Sound" desktop. When there is no sound when using it for the first time, click "Sound Library", click "Try Sample Sounds" in the empty list, wait for the loading to complete, and click "Close" on the upper right to return to the desktop.
blog_layout-sampler.text_044: If the sound library already has your material, this empty state entry may not appear; you can select an existing material to practice, and do not clear your project to match the screenshot.
blog_layout-sampler.attr_045: The synthesized sample sound actually loaded after clicking "Try Sample Sound" from the empty sound library.
blog_layout-sampler.text_046: The synthesized sample sound actually loaded after clicking "Try Sample Sound" from the empty sound library.
blog_layout-sampler.text_047: 2. Click on the kick drum and snare drum to identify the loaded tracks.
blog_layout-sampler.text_048: Tap the "Kick Drum" and "Snare Drum" drum pads that have loaded preset sounds successively. The speakers will play crisp percussion sound effects, and the small screen will simultaneously highlight the name of the currently triggered track.
blog_layout-sampler.text_049: Empty drum pads are in a state to be assigned, which is convenient for subsequent recording or importing custom audio; it cannot be considered that the audio has been loaded just because the grid exists, please look for the drum pads marked with names.
blog_layout-sampler.text_050: 3. Open the sampling menu and enter sound connection and fine tuning.
blog_layout-sampler.text_051: Click the sampling menu entry on the small screen above and select "Sound Connection and Fine Tuning". Double-check the name of the sound you're currently editing at the top of the edit page to make sure it's the one you want to fine-tune.
blog_layout-sampler.text_052: If you select the wrong sound, return to the desktop and re-select the target drum pad. The sampling menu also provides rich access to audition, recording collection and slice production. This exercise first focuses on the attribute calibration of a single audio track.
blog_layout-sampler.attr_053: The small screen sampling menu that is actually clicked.
blog_layout-sampler.text_054: The small screen sampling menu that is actually clicked.
blog_layout-sampler.text_055: 4. Listen to the sound, fine-tune the gain and experience loudness sorting
blog_layout-sampler.text_056: Click "Audio Sound" on the sound editing page, drag the volume slider to make small changes, and listen again to compare the loudness. For sample clips with lower recording levels, you can click "Organize Loudness" to adjust the loudness, and then listen to the changes.
blog_layout-sampler.text_057: Loudness sorting should be used flexibly according to the listening sense of the material to avoid pushing all parameters to the maximum at one time, causing audio overload distortion. If necessary, you can use the undo button to restore the settings.
blog_layout-sampler.attr_058: The sound editing page actually opened, showing the audition, volume and sound connection settings.
blog_layout-sampler.text_059: The sound editing page actually opened, showing the audition, volume and sound connection settings.
blog_layout-sampler.text_060: 5. Configure sound connection: distinguish between overlay playback and relay playback
blog_layout-sampler.text_061: In the "Sound Connection" settings, check the "Overlay Play" and "Relay Play" options. Overlay playback allows multiple pad sounds to sound mixed together at the same time; relay playback (mutually exclusive group) will immediately cut off the tail of the previous sound when a new sound is triggered.
blog_layout-sampler.text_062: After selecting the relay mode, return to the drum pads and alternately hit the two drum pads in the same group to hear the effect. If two sounds are not classified into the same mutually exclusive group, they will not automatically mute each other. Please check the mutually exclusive group assignments on the fine-tuning page.
blog_layout-sampler.text_063: 6. Import custom materials and create slices
blog_layout-sampler.text_064: After mastering sound editing, you can return to the sound recording desktop and click "Import File", or record a short piece of sound from the collection portal. After new material enters the sound library, still follow the sequence of "Select → Audition → Check Name → Adjust".
blog_layout-sampler.text_065: When you want to slice, enter "Cut into several small sounds" from the menu, listen to the boundaries first, and then save the slice. The exported project ZIP is used for backup; there is currently no in-app project package import interface, so do not treat the backup package as a project format that can be directly re-imported.
blog_layout-sampler.text_068: First make sure it has sound bound, then check the device volume, audio output and whether it is still recording. Playback will be paused during microphone collection; sound needs to be added to empty cells first.
blog_layout-sampler.text_070: Presets allow continued addition of sounds. The four samples only occupy part of the space, and the empty space does not mean that the entire sampler is unavailable, nor does it need to be forced to fill up to play.
blog_layout-sampler.text_071: What is the relationship between slices and full soundtracks?
blog_layout-sampler.text_072: Slices record the playback range in the original sound, and the original file is retained. Listen to the slice boundaries before saving; don't interpret on-screen dividing lines to mean that the original audio has been deleted.

blog_layout-smart-home.text_036: Free common home controls from cumbersome app menus. By binding Home Assistant to your smart home layout, you can turn your desk lamp or room light into a knob component with delicate scales, and switch and adjust brightness at the palm of your hand.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_037: The device in the picture is provided by the local demo service, and switching operations will update the demo status. Once you're connected to a real home, check your phone's readback, Home Assistant status, and actual device action at the same time.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_040: Install Naimao Magic Control 1.2.0 on iPhone/iPad. This function can be used independently and does not require connection to a Mac.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_041: Prepare Home Assistant that is already running, and a light that can be controlled normally on the platform. The phone needs to be able to access its address; first verify that the switch is working in Home Assistant itself.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_042: 1. Enter the smart home layout and click on the "Connect Home" portal
blog_layout-smart-home.text_043: Click the "Layouts" tab at the bottom of your iPhone to find and enter the "Smart Home" layout in the list. For multi-desktop solutions, please expand the arrow on the right and select the corresponding desktop.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_044: When entering for the first time and the connection has not been configured yet, the "Connect Home" button will be displayed in the center of the desktop. Click it to enter the Home Connect wizard and select Add Home Assistant service. If the device has been added before, you can manage it directly on the existing connection without having to build the network again.

blog_layout-smart-home.text_046: Home connection management page; there is currently a local demo connection and you can continue to add Home Assistant.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_047: 2. Fill in the Home Assistant service address and long-term access token
blog_layout-smart-home.text_048: Fill in your Home Assistant address in the "Service address" field of the connection form. For example, a local instance might use homeassistant.local:8123, but this must be replaced with an address that the phone can actually access.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_049: Create a long-term access token on the Security page of your Home Assistant profile and copy it into the app's Access Token field. Do not fill in the login password as a token. If using local HTTP, follow the page prompts to confirm "Allow this local HTTP connection"; the token is only used for your own connection, do not include it in the tutorial screenshot.
blog_layout-smart-home.attr_050: The actual Home Assistant connection form that opens; the tutorial screenshot does not fill in the real access token.

blog_layout-smart-home.text_053: Home Assistant official profile and security settings instructions
blog_layout-smart-home.text_054: 3. After the connection is successful, add the smart lighting component to the desktop
blog_layout-smart-home.text_055: Click "Connect" and wait for a clear connected status and device list. Click "Return to Layout, Add Component", then enter the editor from "Add Equipment Component" in the empty layout, select the home equipment component and bind the lamp just now.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_056: You can also use the "Automatically add... online devices" entry on the empty desktop to join in batches. The successful connection and the component being added are two steps; just filling in the token will not allow each device to automatically appear on the existing desktop.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_057: 4. Check the device name and room, click the switch in the center of the knob
blog_layout-smart-home.text_058: Save the desktop and return to the main interface, check the device name on the card and the room it belongs to (such as "desk lamp/study"). Tap the center area of ​​the light knob to send an on-off command, observe the status changes of the center indicator light, and confirm in the real room that the physical lamps have been turned off or on simultaneously.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_059: The phone will wait for Home Assistant's real status readback and update the UI. The instantaneous animation of button press is only touch feedback. Please refer to the actual physical lamp or status readback.

blog_layout-smart-home.text_062: 5. Press and hold the outer ring of the knob to adjust the light brightness smoothly
blog_layout-smart-home.text_063: The center of the light knob is responsible for turning the power on and off, and the outer ring is responsible for dimming. Press and hold the outer ring of the knob and slowly rotate it clockwise to increase the brightness, rotate it counterclockwise to decrease the brightness, and wait for the status value to be read back after letting go.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_064: First make small adjustments to confirm that the light and dark changes of the physical lamp are consistent with the percentage value displayed on the mobile phone. The dimming function requires that the lamp hardware itself supports the dimming protocol. Ordinary on-off sockets only support switch operations.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_065: 6. Click the device name to view details and expand the smart ecosystem of the whole house

blog_layout-smart-home.text_067: When the switch and readback of a light are verified, add curtains, sockets and other equipment, and check their true actions one by one. blog_layout-smart-home.text_072: First check if Home Connection finds supported devices, then return to the layout to add and bind home device components. Existing connections will not automatically rearrange your previously edited desktop.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_073: Why is the button grayed out when the status shows offline?
blog_layout-smart-home.text_074: Offline devices are not guaranteed to receive control requests. First check the online status in the home platform and the connection from the mobile phone to the service address; after recovery, wait for the new status to be read back.
blog_layout-smart-home.text_075: Can I switch to Apple Home?
blog_layout-smart-home.text_076: You can connect to an existing Apple home and follow the system prompts to allow access. The device needs to be added and available on the home platform first; capabilities such as cameras and door locks are not supported by the lighting exercises in this article.

blog_layout-terminal.text_036: No need to keep a terminal window stacked in front of your home screen when compiling code or monitoring services. The terminal layout allows you to easily create and manage multiple Shell tabs on your mobile phone, receive terminal output in real time, and expand it to full screen to immerse yourself in input and browse history, making control of background tasks easier and more casual.
blog_layout-terminal.text_037: This time, the new creation, renaming and full-screen operations are actually completed in the native terminal interface. The output in the screenshot is provided by Terminal Preview mode and is not a log of this remote command execution; the read-only commands below need to be run in your paired Mac session.
blog_layout-terminal.text_040: Install Naimao Control on iPhone/iPad, and install the corresponding companion terminal on Mac; complete LAN pairing, and allow accessibility permissions on the Mac terminal. When you need the computer screen, turn on the screen recording permission.
blog_layout-terminal.text_041: The Mac companion needs to be running to support native shell sessions. When practicing, it is recommended to use a temporary session without important processes first, and do not close a session that is running time-consuming tasks.
blog_layout-terminal.text_042: 1. Enter the terminal layout and get to know the session tab bar at the top
blog_layout-terminal.text_043: Click the "Layouts" tab at the bottom of your iPhone, find and enter the "Terminal" layout in the list. When there are many layouts, you can quickly search through the search box at the top.
blog_layout-terminal.text_044: Above the small screen are conversation tabs. The "Development" "Service" in the screenshot is from demo mode; when you first connect, you may not have any sessions yet. Don't think of these two names as configurations that must be created in advance.
blog_layout-terminal.attr_045: Compact terminal interface: both sessions and output are clear preview data.
blog_layout-terminal.text_046: Compact terminal interface: both sessions and output are clear preview data.
blog_layout-terminal.text_047: 2. Click the plus sign to create a new session and wait for the prompt to be ready.
blog_layout-terminal.text_048: Click the "+" button on the right side of the session bar and wait for the new terminal session label to be created and highlighted. The Mac side will allocate and start a new Shell instance simultaneously.
blog_layout-terminal.text_049: Wait for the terminal prompt (such as $ or %) to appear stably before proceeding, so as to avoid accumulating redundant empty sessions due to short-term network fluctuations and rapid clicking of the plus sign.
blog_layout-terminal.attr_050: The Shell 3 tab appears after actually clicking New; preview mode provides sample output.
blog_layout-terminal.text_051: The Shell 3 tab appears after actually clicking New; preview mode provides sample output.
blog_layout-terminal.text_052: 3. Open the terminal menu and rename the practice session to Build
blog_layout-terminal.text_053: Click on the "Terminal Menu" and select the "Rename" option. In the pop-up edit box, replace the default Shell 1 with the easily identifiable "Build" and click "Save" to confirm.
blog_layout-terminal.text_054: The top label will be updated to Build. This name is only used as a friendly label for mobile session management and will not change any local file directories on Mac or execute any background commands.
blog_layout-terminal.attr_055: The actual interface after the new session is renamed Build.
blog_layout-terminal.text_056: The actual interface after the new session is renamed Build.
blog_layout-terminal.text_057: 4. Expand the terminal in full screen and run the read-only command to verify the link.
blog_layout-terminal.text_058: Click the full-screen expansion button of the terminal component, and then click the keyboard icon in the full-screen interface. Enter the read-only check command into your phone's keyboard
blog_layout-terminal.text_059: And press Enter to view the current working path of your Mac.
blog_layout-terminal.text_062: And press Enter, confirm that the next line is clearly echoed in the terminal output area.
blog_layout-terminal.text_063: , verify that the two-way character transmission link is completely normal and has no garbled characters.
blog_layout-terminal.attr_066: The actual interface for a full-screen terminal; uses the same session as the compact page.
blog_layout-terminal.text_067: The actual interface for a full-screen terminal; uses the same session as the compact page.
blog_layout-terminal.text_068: 5. Switch the session label and confirm that the historical output is persisted
blog_layout-terminal.text_069: Put away the phone keyboard, click on other session tabs at the top to switch, and then switch back to the "Build" session to check whether the historical output of the command just executed is intact.
blog_layout-terminal.text_070: Click "Finish" in the upper right corner to exit full-screen mode. The terminal status in the small screen will still be synchronized in real time, and the background Shell process will not be interrupted abnormally when leaving the terminal layout.
blog_layout-terminal.text_071: 6. Safely end the practice session and release system resources
blog_layout-terminal.text_072: After the exercise, if you do not need to keep the temporary session, first confirm that there are no time-consuming compilation or service processes running in the session, then open "Terminal Menu → Close Session" and click Confirm in the secondary confirmation panel.
blog_layout-terminal.text_073: At this point the Build tag is safely removed and the corresponding session on the Mac is properly cleaned up. If you just want to hide the keyboard temporarily, click Keyboard Hide or "Done" without closing the entire session.
blog_layout-terminal.text_076: First check whether it prompts "Connect to Mac and then use Terminal" or "Please update Mac to use Terminal". Check the companion version and number of sessions if the connection is still unavailable; up to eight sessions per mobile device.
blog_layout-terminal.text_077: The text layout has changed after full screen. Did you open a new terminal?

blog_layout-work.text_036: Place your phone flat next to your Mac keyboard, and the work layout becomes your exclusive physical sub-console. blog_layout-work.text_041: Open a blank document in TextEdit on Mac and click on the text to make the insertion cursor visible. Don't practice on the password box, file name, or chat send box yet.
blog_layout-work.text_042: 1. Open "Work" and confirm the operation goal
blog_layout-work.text_043: Click "Layout" at the bottom of the app and find "Jobs" in the list. blog_layout-work.text_044: There's a trackpad, mouse wheel, live keyboard, and keys for copy, paste, undo, redo, and more. blog_layout-work.text_046: Work desktop: Use the demo connection this time; first place the cursor in the Mac document when practicing.
blog_layout-work.text_047: 2. Click "Live Keyboard" and enter a line of practice text
blog_layout-work.text_048: Click "Live Keyboard" on the work desktop to open the input panel, and then click "Live" above the panel. The app remembers the last mode used, so it checks the selection first each time. The real-time mode will send text to the Mac as the keyboard is entered; first enter the short sentence "Write an outline first today" and observe whether the same content appears in the Mac document.
blog_layout-work.text_049: When inputting Chinese, complete the candidate word selection first, and then check the words in the document. If the text falls into other windows, stop typing first and re-click the text on your Mac. Do not send it continuously.

blog_layout-work.text_052: 3. Return to the work desktop and try to undo it once
blog_layout-work.text_053: Click "Done" on the input panel, return to the work desktop, and then click "Undo". This key press sends Command-Z, and the actual undo unit is determined by the text editor: it may undo one word at a time, or it may undo a block of input.
blog_layout-work.text_054: After seeing clearly what just disappeared, click "Redo" once. Redo Send Shift-Command-Z; don't take this to mean that all software has the same operating history.
blog_layout-work.text_056: Select the sentence just now in the Mac document, return to the phone and click "Copy". Then start a new line on your Mac, make sure the selection is deselected and the insertion point is in place, and then click "Paste" on your phone.
blog_layout-work.text_057: Check if the new line is the same text. "Copy" and "Paste" correspond to Mac's Command-C and Command-V respectively, and use the Mac clipboard; they will not automatically put text into the phone's clipboard.
blog_layout-work.text_058: 5. Find the editing entrance of the current desktop
blog_layout-work.text_059: When you need to adjust these keys, click "Layout" at the bottom, and then click "Edit Current Desktop". After the page enters the layout editor, first observe the position of each component; this exercise does not require moving or deleting any components. Click "Finish" to return to the control desktop.
blog_layout-work.text_060: If you want to add a frequently used button in the future, you can start here without having to create another working layout.
