blog_remote-control-mac.text_034: Based on the direct point-to-point connection of the local LAN, you can monitor the Mac desktop, control the cursor, scroll smoothly with two fingers on your mobile device by just scanning the QR code, and supports draft editing and real-time key input.
blog_remote-control-mac.text_035: After connecting to your Mac, try cursor movement and text input in a blank document. When you need to view the computer screen, turn on the screen preview.
blog_remote-control-mac.text_036: Let’s do a little exercise first:
blog_remote-control-mac.text_037: 1. LAN screen monitoring and point-to-point transmission
blog_remote-control-mac.text_038: First run NinoPad on both ends, connect to a mutually accessible LAN and complete pairing. Moving the cursor and entering text require Mac accessibility permissions; viewing the desktop screen also requires screen recording permissions. After connecting, first open a test window on your Mac, and then see if the phone preview corresponds to this window.
blog_remote-control-mac.text_039: 2. Two display modes: control while watching and full-screen viewing
blog_remote-control-mac.text_040: For different operation scenarios, NinoPad provides flexible viewports and operation layouts:
blog_remote-control-mac.text_041: 1. Watch and control on the desktop
blog_remote-control-mac.text_042: The upper half of the phone screen uses a small window to monitor the focus area of the Mac desktop in real time, while the lower half is concentrated on a large virtual touchpad, stepless scroll bars and commonly used shortcut actions. It is especially suitable for holding the phone with one hand, monitoring the rendering or compilation progress, and blindly operating the cursor and scroll wheel.
blog_remote-control-mac.text_044: When a larger preview is required, use the full-screen entry in the screen preview area. After expanding, make sure you see the target window; after returning to the desktop, continue using the trackpad, scrolling, and common keys. On-screen feedback still needs to correspond to the actual window on your Mac.
blog_remote-control-mac.attr_045: NinoPad displays Mac screen in full screen
blog_remote-control-mac.text_046: Full-screen mode: Presents a complete macOS desktop screen, intuitively supporting multi-touch and gesture interaction
blog_remote-control-mac.text_048: NinoPad brings the core interaction logic of Apple Magic Trackpad to the touch screen:
blog_remote-control-mac.text_049: Smoothly position the cursor and support adaptive acceleration curve;
blog_remote-control-mac.text_051: A single finger tap corresponds to a left mouse click, and a two-finger tap directly brings up the contextual right-click menu;
blog_remote-control-mac.text_053: Two-finger smooth scrolling with natural inertia damping makes browsing long web pages and codes easy and smooth;
blog_remote-control-mac.text_054: Swipe up and down with two fingers:
blog_remote-control-mac.text_055: Easily drag the window title bar, select a text area, or move timeline elements with one hand.
blog_remote-control-mac.text_056: Double click and long press and drag:
blog_remote-control-mac.text_057: 4. Dual-mode keyboard architecture: draft pre-editing vs real-time terminal input
blog_remote-control-mac.text_058: For different input scenarios, NinoPad provides two distinct keyboard input modes:
blog_remote-control-mac.text_059: Suitable for writing long texts, replying to messages, and organizing meeting shorthand. Make full use of the input method and speech-to-text tools on the mobile phone. After repeatedly checking and confirming that it is correct, click "Up Screen" and the entire text will be accurately delivered to the current focus cursor on the Mac at once.
blog_remote-control-mac.text_061: Specially optimized for terminal command line, code debugging and shortcut key combinations. Each key input (e.g.
blog_remote-control-mac.text_065: , arrow keys and Enter) are all sent to the current input position of the Mac on the fly.

blog_voice-text-input.text_031: Dictate the draft first, proofread it on your phone, and then securely send it to your Mac · Read about 5 minutes
blog_voice-text-input.attr_032: NinoPad text keyboard and voice input interface
blog_voice-text-input.text_033: When writing long articles, replying to messages, or organizing meeting minutes, voice input directly on the computer is prone to input errors due to environmental noise or homophone recognition errors. NinoPad adopts the design concept of "first draft on the mobile phone, proofread it correctly, and then send it with one click", taking into account both speed and accuracy.
blog_voice-text-input.text_034: First switch to draft mode, then dictate, revise, and finally input to Mac. Place the cursor in the text on your computer before sending.
blog_voice-text-input.text_036: 1. The difference between text draft mode and real-time keystrokes
blog_voice-text-input.text_037: Designed specifically for long paragraphs and oral shorthand. The text is only temporarily stored locally on the mobile phone. After clicking the "Up Screen" button, the entire text is delivered to the current focus cursor on the Mac at one time to avoid disturbing the computer cursor while recognizing it.
blog_voice-text-input.text_038: Text mode: Edit the draft first:
blog_voice-text-input.text_039: Designed specifically for terminal commands and shortcut keys, every keystroke (such as
blog_voice-text-input.text_043: Live mode: Transfer to Mac as you type:
blog_voice-text-input.text_044: 2. The four-step process of voice shorthand and proofreading
blog_voice-text-input.text_045: Enter the input panel from the "Live Keyboard" on the work desktop and click "Text" at the top. The app will remember the last mode used. Make sure "Text" is selected before typing in the draft area.
blog_voice-text-input.text_047: Click the "Microphone" button at the bottom of the interface to call the iOS system's speech recognition engine to transcribe the spoken content into text in real time (networking and offline processing of speech recognition depend on the iOS system version and language settings).
blog_voice-text-input.text_048: Tap the microphone to start dictating:
blog_voice-text-input.text_049: Click the microphone again to stop recording. Correct typos, fine-tune segmentation and punctuation directly on the touch screen of your phone.
blog_voice-text-input.text_050: Check and modify on mobile phone:
blog_voice-text-input.text_051: Place the cursor in the text of the Mac test document, and then click the upward arrow ("up screen") on the mobile phone input panel. Check that text appears where expected; it only handles typing and does not choose chat partners or submit messages for you.
blog_voice-text-input.text_053: 3. Frequently used copy loading and one-click clearing
blog_voice-text-input.text_054: Click "History" in the input panel to retrieve the previous text and fill it back into the draft, and then display it on the screen after modification. Before clearing the draft, make sure that the required content has been retained to avoid clearing out unused text.

ui.answer_network_question: Can I control my Mac over the internet?
ui.answer_network_body: NinoPad controls a paired Mac over the same local network. It does not provide internet remote desktop or a cloud relay. Both devices need a reachable local Wi-Fi network; guest-network isolation can prevent pairing.
ui.answer_requirements_question: Which devices and systems do I need?
ui.answer_requirements_body: Use iOS / iPadOS 17 or later and the free Mac companion on macOS 13 or later, with Apple Silicon or Intel. Input control requires Accessibility permission; screen mirroring also requires Screen Recording permission.
ui.answer_free_question: What is free, and what does Pro unlock?
ui.answer_free_body: Basic keypad and system controls are free. Pro unlocks advanced decks, custom dynamic wallpapers and standalone instruments. Weekly, annual and lifetime plans provide the same Pro features; see the App Store checkout for local prices.

Website analytics is separate from the app’s local control data. Advertising personalization, Google signals and cross-app tracking are not enabled.
privacy.growth_analytics_controls: Decline or withdraw consent through Analytics preferences in the footer. Browser Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control signals prevent analytics from loading.
